signals.title: ip_tagging integration test: make LDS update counter wait non-racy
signals.text: `IpTaggingIntegrationTest.IptaggingFilterWithReloadNoCrashOnLdsUpdate` was flaky because it waited for a monotonically increasing counter with `Eq(1)`, which can never match if the value advances to `2` before polling starts. This updates the wait to assert a lower bound instead of an exact value. - **What changed** - In `test/extensions/filters/http/ip_tagging/ip_tagging_integration_test.cc`, changed: - `listener_manager.lds.update_success` matcher from `testing::Eq(1)` to `testing::Ge(1)` inside `IptaggingFilterWithReloadNoCrashOnLdsUpdate`. - No other code paths or tests were modified. - **Why this resolves the flake** - The test already gates on listener state (`total_listeners_active == 1`, `total_listeners_draining == 0`), so requiring **at least one** successful LDS update is the correct invariant and avoids races on counter increments. ```cpp test_server_->waitForCounter("listener_manager.lds.update_success", testing::Ge(1)); ``` > [!WARNING] > > <details> > <summary>Firewall rules blocked me from connecting to one or more addresses (expand for details)</summary> > > #### I tried to connect to the following addresses, but was blocked by firewall rules: > > - `ftpmirror.gnu.org` > - Triggering command: `/build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/embedded_tools/jdk/bin/java bazel(envoy) --add-opens=java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -Xverify:none -Djava.util.logging.config.file=/build/bazel_root/base/javalog.properties -Dcom.google.devtools.build.lib.util.LogHandlerQuerier.class=com.google.devtools.build.lib.util.SimpleLogHandler$HandlerQuerier -XX:-MaxFDLimit -Djava.library.path=/build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/embedded_tools/jdk/lib:/build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/embedded_tools/jdk/lib/server:/build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/ -Dfile.encoding=ISO-8859-1 -Duser.country= -Duser.language= -Duser.variant= -Xmx3g -DBAZEL_TRACK_SOURCE_DIRECTORIES=1 -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/tmp/custom-cacerts -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit -jar /build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/A-server.jar --max_idle_secs=10800 --noshutdown_on_low_sys_mem --connect_timeout_secs=30` (dns block) > - `mirror.bazel.build` > - Triggering command: `/build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/embedded_tools/jdk/bin/java bazel(envoy) --add-opens=java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -Xverify:none -Djava.util.logging.config.file=/build/bazel_root/base/javalog.properties -Dcom.google.devtools.build.lib.util.LogHandlerQuerier.class=com.google.devtools.build.lib.util.SimpleLogHandler$HandlerQuerier -XX:-MaxFDLimit -Djava.library.path=/build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/embedded_tools/jdk/lib:/build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/embedded_tools/jdk/lib/server:/build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/ -Dfile.encoding=ISO-8859-1 -Duser.country= -Duser.language= -Duser.variant= -Xmx3g -DBAZEL_TRACK_SOURCE_DIRECTORIES=1 -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/tmp/custom-cacerts -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit -jar /build/bazel_root/install/fb2a7f6d344d2f4e335882534df59296/A-server.jar --max_idle_secs=10800 --noshutdown_on_low_sys_mem --connect_timeout_secs=30` (dns block) > > If you need me to access, download, or install something from one of these locations, you can either: > > - Configure [Actions setup steps](https://gh.io/copilot/actions-setup-steps) to set up my environment, which run before the firewall is enabled > - Add the appropriate URLs or hosts to the custom allowlist in this repository's [Copilot coding agent settings](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/settings/copilot/coding_agent) (admins only) > > </details> <!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT --> <details> <summary>Original prompt</summary> ## Problem The integration test `IpTaggingIntegrationTest.IptaggingFilterWithReloadNoCrashOnLdsUpdate` (added recently in #38574) is flaky in CI. Observed failure: ``` [ RUN ] IpVersions/IpTaggingIntegrationTest.IptaggingFilterWithReloadNoCrashOnLdsUpdate/0 ./test/integration/server.h:474: Failure Value of: TestUtility::waitForCounter(statStore(), name, value_matcher, time_system_, timeout, dispatcher) Actual: false (timed out waiting for listener_manager.lds.update_success to is equal to 1: current value 2) Expected: true ``` ## Root cause At https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/blob/main/test/extensions/filters/http/ip_tagging/ip_tagging_integration_test.cc#L168 the test does: ```cpp test_server_->waitForCounter("listener_manager.lds.update_success", testing::Eq(1)); ``` Counters in Envoy are monotonically increasing. `waitForCounter` polls the counter against the matcher and gives up on a timeout. Using `testing::Eq(1)` is racy: if the counter has already advanced past 1 (in the observed failure it was already 2) by the time the wait starts, the equality matcher can never be satisfied and the wait will always time out. This race is easy to hit because `initialize()` itself can produce an `lds.update_success` tick before the subsequent `setLds("1")` increments it again, so the counter can race from 0 → 2 before the test thread starts waiting. The companion test `FileBasedIpTaggingWithReload` in the same file already uses the correct idiom (`testing::Ge(2)`) for a similar counter wait — the new test just used `Eq` by oversight. ## Fix Change the matcher from `testing::Eq(1)` to `testing::Ge(1)` on line 168 of `test/extensions/filters/http/ip_tagging/ip_tagging_integration_test.cc`. The surrounding waits on `listener_manager.total_listeners_active == 1` and `listener_manager.total_listeners_draining == 0` already establish that the LDS update has been applied and the old listener has finished draining, so `Ge(1)` is sufficient — we just need to ensure at least one successful LDS update has been observed, not exactly one. ## Acceptance criteria - Update line 168 of `test/extensions/filters/http/ip_tagging/ip_tagging_integration_test.cc` to use `testing::Ge(1)` instead of `testing::Eq(1)`. - Do not change anything else. - Keep the commit minimal and focused; include `Signed-off-by` as the project requires. ## Release notes This is a test-only change. No release notes / changelog entry is needed (the feature itself was just added in #38574 and has not shipped). The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated): User: ``` [ RUN ] IpVersions/IpTaggingIntegrationTest.IptaggingFilterWithReloadNoCrashOnLdsUpdate/0 ./test/integration/server.h:474: Failure Value of: TestUtility::waitForCounter(statStore(), name, value_matcher, time_system_, timeout, dispatcher) Actual: false (timed out waiting for listener_manager.lds.update_success to is equal to 1: current value 2) Expected: true Stack trace: 0xaaaaaf702934: Envoy::IntegrationTestServer::waitForCounter() 0xaaaaaf4d7048: Envoy::(anonymous namespace)::IpTaggingIntegrationTest_IptaggingFilterWithReloadNoCrashOnLdsUpdate_Test::TestBody() 0xaaaab0bc5c90: testing::internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported<>() 0xaaaab0bc5b2c: testing::Test::Run() 0xaaaab0bc6cf8: testing::TestInfo::Run() ... Google Test internal frames ... Error: 5-20 06:23:22.299][6859][error][conf ``` thisi is a reccently added flake that im seeing around quite a bit (just tyring to repro) im minded to revert given it was recent - unless the fix is obvious (and need to actually track the culprit) Assistant: Looking at the failure, the test was just added in PR #38574 (merged 2026-05-18 by @nezdolik). The flake is at line 168: ```cpp test_server_->waitForCounter("listener_manager.lds.update_success", testing::Eq(1)); ``` Failure says: *"timed out waiting for listener_manager.lds.update_success to is equal to 1: current value 2"*. This is a classic race. `waitForCounter` polls a monotonically-increasing counter against `Eq(1)`. Counters only go up, so once the value has been observed at 2 the `Eq(1)` matcher can never be satisfied — it can only time out. What's happening: - `initialize()` brings the server up. Depending on timing/integration-test plumbing, that itself can already cause `listener_manager.lds.update_success` to tick (the bootstrap is parsed and a listener is added) — and `setLds("1")` then increments it again. - On the fast path the counter blows past 1 to 2 before the wait starts → permanent timeout. The pattern in this same file at line 99 (the older test added in the same PR) already uses the correct idiom — `testing::Ge(2)` rather than `Eq`. The new test inadvertently used `Eq`. ### Suggested fix (minimal) Change line 168 to use `Ge`: ```cpp name=test/extensions/filters/http/ip_tagging/ip_tagging_integration_test.cc url=https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/blob/b5c0d52f1b6be631be7... </details> <!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX --> *This pull request was created from Copilot chat.* >

signals.title: internal_upstream: reverse-propagate filter state across the internal listener boundary at close
signals.text: # internal_upstream: reverse-propagate filter state across the internal listener boundary at close ## Commit Message internal_upstream: reverse-propagate filter state across the internal listener boundary at close ## Additional Description When an internal listener is used (cluster `transport_socket: envoy.transport_sockets.internal_upstream` → `tunneling_encap_listener` → tcp_proxy), the userspace IoHandle pair currently propagates dynamic metadata and filter state objects *forward* (downstream → internal-listener stream) at connection creation via `PassthroughState::initialize`/`mergeInto`. There is no reverse path: filter state produced on the inner side never crosses back to the outer (downstream) side. This is the first piece of a fix for #43977 — propagating a non-2xx CONNECT response status (e.g. a `tcp_proxy` upstream tunnel that returns 403) from the inner side back to the downstream HCM, so operators see the real upstream status instead of a canonical 503. This change is the *primitive* only. It introduces: - A new `StreamSharingMayImpactPooling::SharedWithDownstreamConnectionOnClose` enum variant, symmetric to the existing `SharedWithUpstreamConnection`. Marks filter state objects that should flow upstream → downstream at upstream close. - `FilterState::objectsSharedWithDownstreamConnectionOnClose()` accessor (parent-chain walk identical to `objectsSharedWithUpstreamConnection`). - `PassthroughState::captureReverse(FilterState&)` and `PassthroughState::mergeReverse(FilterState&)`. `captureReverse` is called on the inner side at connection close to harvest marked objects into the shared `PassthroughState`. `mergeReverse` is called on the outer side at its own close to deposit them into its connection's filter state. Names already present on the recipient are overwritten (last-writer-wins), matching the forward `mergeInto`. - `IoHandle::addOnPreCloseCallback`. `IoHandleImpl::close()` fires registered callbacks exactly once, before notifying the peer or tearing down the file event. This is the hook the inner side uses to call `captureReverse` while its connection's StreamInfo is still queryable. - Wiring on both sides of the boundary: - Inner side: `ActiveInternalListener::newActiveConnection` registers a pre-close callback that calls `captureReverse(connection.streamInfo().filterState())`, capturing the `FilterStateSharedPtr` by value so the callback is safe even if it fires from the IoHandle destructor (i.e. after the Connection is gone). - Outer side: `InternalSocket::closeSocket` calls `mergeReverse(connection.streamInfo().filterState())` before delegating to the base `PassthroughSocket::closeSocket`. - One concrete consumer: `TunnelingConfigHelperImpl::propagateResponseHeaders` and `propagateResponseTrailers` now set their filter state objects with `SharedWithDownstreamConnectionOnClose`. With `propagate_response_headers: true` on the inner `tcp_proxy`, the captured response headers/trailers are now reverse-propagated to the downstream connection's filter state automatically. The primitive is general: any inner-side network or HTTP filter can mark a filter state object with the new flag to opt into reverse propagation. ### captureReverse is idempotent (close-ordering robustness) The reverse channel relies on `captureReverse` (inner/accepted side, at close) running before `mergeReverse` (outer/InternalSocket side, at close). That close ordering is not guaranteed: on a client-initiated teardown the outer side closes first, so `mergeReverse` finalizes the shared `PassthroughState` before `captureReverse` runs. `captureReverse` therefore captures only while still in its initial state (mirroring the re-entry tolerance `mergeReverse` already has) instead of asserting single invocation; first-state-wins is correct because when merge precedes capture there is nothing to propagate. Without this, existing `InternalUpstreamIntegrationTest` cases abort on close. Reverse propagation is thus effective in the inner-closes-first ordering (the intended `tcp_proxy` non-2xx-CONNECT path). Making it order-independent (capturing eagerly when the object is set, rather than at close) is left as a follow-up. ### What's *not* in this PR - Plumbing the propagated filter state through `Router::UpstreamRequest::onPoolFailure` (currently it only flows through `onPoolReady` via `setUpstreamFilterState`). On the failure path, `streamInfo:upstreamFilterState()` and `%UPSTREAM_FILTER_STATE%` still see nothing. That fix is intended as a separate follow-up PR — it widens the connection pool callback API and is structurally bigger than this primitive. - Lua/access-log accessors beyond the existing surface. Existing `%UPSTREAM_FILTER_STATE(envoy.tcp_proxy.propagate_response_headers:TYPED)%` continues to work on the success path; the failure-path fix is in the followup. - Any change to the wire-level behavior of `tcp_proxy` itself (CONNECT semantics, reset behavior, retries). ## Risk Level Low. - The new enum variant is opt-in. No existing filter state objects set this flag, so no existing behavior changes. - The `IoHandle::addOnPreCloseCallback` interface is new and has zero existing registrations outside this PR's wiring; the close path's behavior is unchanged when the callback list is empty. - The change to `propagateResponseHeaders`/`propagateResponseTrailers` requires `propagate_response_headers: true` (already opt-in) to fire at all. With the option off, the call is a no-op as before. With the option on, the only observable difference is that the captured `TunnelResponseHeaders` filter state object additionally appears on the downstream connection's filter state at upstream close — operators get *more* information, not different information. - The reverse-merge is last-writer-wins, matching the forward mergeInto. Only objects explicitly marked with the new opt-in flag propagate, so no unrelated downstream filter state is touched.. ## Testing - Existing `propagate_response_headers` integration tests cover the inner-side access-log path; the change to `propagateResponseHeaders`/`propagateResponseTrailers` only adds an opt-in sharing flag to `setData` and does not alter the data placed on the inner-side filter state. - New unit tests in `test/extensions/io_socket/user_space/io_handle_impl_test.cc` exercising `captureReverse` → `mergeReverse` with a marked filter state object. - New unit tests in `test/extensions/transport_sockets/internal_upstream/internal_upstream_test.cc` verifying `InternalSocket::closeSocket` invokes `mergeReverse` exactly once and passes the right filter state. - Validated end-to-end on a private envoy deployment in a real-traffic test environment: an inner `tcp_proxy` CONNECT receiving a 403 from its upstream now lands a `TunnelResponseHeaders` filter state object (with the propagated `:status`) on the downstream connection's filter state. Without the patch, the downstream connection's filter state is empty for this case. - New integration test in `test/extensions/transport_sockets/internal_upstream/internal_upstream_integration_test.cc`: an outer HCM → internal-listener → inner tcp_proxy that CONNECT-tunnels and receives a non-2xx response; asserts the captured response-headers filter state object is readable on the downstream HCM via `%UPSTREAM_FILTER_STATE(envoy.tcp_proxy.propagate_response_headers:TYPED)%`. Also guards the close-ordering fix — it reproduces the existing-suite abort without the `captureReverse` idempotency change. ## Docs Changes `api/envoy/extensions/filters/network/tcp_proxy/v3/tcp_proxy.proto` updated to note that when `propagate_response_headers`/`propagate_response_trailers` are true and the tcp_proxy is on the inner side of an internal-listener boundary, the resulting filter state objects also become available on the downstream (outer-side) connection's filter state at upstream close. No new config fields. ## Release Notes Added as `changelogs/current/new_features/` fragments (the changelog was migrated from the monolithic `current.yaml` to per-entry `.rst` files): `tcp_proxy__reverse-propagate-across-internal-listener.rst`: > tcp_proxy: when ``propagate_response_headers`` or ``propagate_response_trailers`` is enabled and the tcp_proxy sits on the inner side of an internal-listener boundary, the captured response headers/trailers filter state object is now additionally reverse-propagated to the outer (downstream) connection's filter state at upstream close. Operators reading filter state from the downstream side via ``%UPSTREAM_FILTER_STATE(envoy.tcp_proxy.propagate_response_headers:TYPED)%`` (or equivalent) on the success path will now also see the value when the inner upstream returns a non-2xx response on CONNECT. A pre-existing object of the same name is overwritten (last-writer-wins), consistent with forward propagation. `filter_state__shared-with-downstream-connection-on-close.rst`: > filter state: added ``StreamSharingMayImpactPooling::SharedWithDownstreamConnectionOnClose`` for marking filter state objects that should be reverse-propagated from the upstream (inner-side) to the downstream (outer-side) connection at upstream close. Currently honored across the internal-listener boundary by ``PassthroughState`` / ``InternalSocket``. ## Platform Specific Features N/A. ## Fixes #43977

signals.title: changelogs: migrate stray current.yaml entries to per-entry layout and delete the file
signals.text: `changelogs/current.yaml` is silently ignored by the toolshed entries-layout (which reads exclusively from `current/**/*.rst` when the `current/` directory exists). Three entries sitting in that file were never migrated and would have been dropped from any release. ## Changes - **New** `changelogs/current/behavior_changes/tls__deprecated-enforce-rsa-key-usage.rst` — migrates the `enforce_rsa_key_usage` deprecation entry; also creates the `behavior_changes/` subdirectory (valid section per `changelogs.yaml`) - **New** `changelogs/current/new_features/network_ext_proc__added-close-stream-to-ext-proc-server.rst` — migrates the `close_stream_to_ext_proc_server` feature entry - **Dropped** the duplicate `network_ext_proc` untyped-metadata entry from `current.yaml` — an identical file already existed at `current/new_features/network_ext_proc__added-support-for-receiving-untyped.rst` - **Deleted** `changelogs/current.yaml` — dead weight; toolshed never reads it in entries-layout mode - **`changelogs/BUILD`** — removed the now-nonexistent `"current.yaml"` from the `changelogs` filegroup `srcs` Note: a follow-up CI guard (rejecting a stray `current.yaml` when entries-layout is active) belongs in `envoy.code.check`'s changelog checker in toolshed and will be handled in a separate PR. <!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT --> <details> <summary>Original prompt</summary> ## Background Envoy moved to a "file-per-entry" changelog scheme, where each changelog entry is a single `.rst` file under: ``` changelogs/current/<section>/<area>__<slug>.rst ``` The valid sections and areas are defined in `changelogs/changelogs.yaml`. The in-flight changelog is now assembled entirely from these per-entry files. The old `changelogs/current.yaml` file is **no longer used**. This has been confirmed against the toolshed pytooling (`envoy.base.utils`): when `changelogs/current/` exists as a directory (the "entries layout"), the changelog data is read exclusively from the per-entry `.rst` files, the release tooling (`write_version`) builds `changelogs/<version>.yaml` from the entry directory, and `current.yaml` is never read or written. Therefore any entries left in `changelogs/current.yaml` are silently ignored and will not appear in any release. Currently `changelogs/current.yaml` still exists and contains 3 stray entries that were never migrated (one of which is an exact duplicate of an existing per-entry file). They must be migrated to the new layout and the file removed. ## Required changes ### 1. signals.text: `main` regressed below the `source/common/upstream` coverage threshold after optional `http_status_code` reporting was added to health-check events. The newly added lines are **only executed when `http_status_code != 0`**, and there is no test that drives the *real* `HealthCheckEventLoggerImpl` with a non-zero status code. The uncovered lines are the two `set_http_status_code(...)` calls: ```cpp // in logEjectUnhealthy(...) if (http_status_code != 0) { event.mutable_eject_unhealthy_event()->set_http_status_code( static_cast<uint32_t>(http_status_code)); } // in logUnhealthy(...) if (http_status_code != 0) { event.mutable_health_check_failure_event()->set_http_status_code( static_cast<uint32_t>(http_status_code)); } ``` The HTTP/gRPC/TCP health-checker tests *do* pass non-zero codes, but only to a **mock** event logger (e.g. `EXPECT_CALL(event_logger_, logEjectUnhealthy(_, _, envoy::data::core::v3::ACTIVE, 503))`), so the concrete logger code path never runs. signals.title: Patch spdlog to force external fmt in Android AAR builds
signals.text: The Android `envoy.aar` CI build was failing in `spdlog` headers after the mobile toolchain selected `std::format` codepaths that are not supported in this build configuration. This change forces Envoy's existing external-`fmt` integration to win for the vendored `spdlog` dependency. - **Root cause** - `spdlog` 1.17.0 checks `SPDLOG_USE_STD_FORMAT` before `SPDLOG_FMT_EXTERNAL`. - In the mobile Android build, that allows `spdlog` to enter `std::format` paths and fail on symbols such as `std::make_format_args`, `std::vformat_to`, and `std::system_error`. - **Change** - Add a small patch for the external `spdlog` archive that undefines `SPDLOG_USE_STD_FORMAT` when `SPDLOG_FMT_EXTERNAL` is already set. - Wire that patch into the Bazel external dependency definition for `spdlog`. - **Effect** - Keeps Envoy on the intended `fmt` backend for logging. - Avoids touching Envoy logging callsites or changing mobile build logic outside dependency selection. ```diff +#if defined(SPDLOG_FMT_EXTERNAL) && defined(SPDLOG_USE_STD_FORMAT) +#undef SPDLOG_USE_STD_FORMAT +#endif ```

signals.title: tools/dependency: harden cve_fetch against transient NVD failures
signals.text: The scheduled `Envoy/CVE` refresh has been failing when the NVD API drops chunked responses mid-stream, causing `aiohttp` payload/connection errors to escape `fetch_page` and abort the run. The downloader also was not actually enforcing `MAX_CONCURRENCY` because it created a new semaphore on each access. - **Concurrency control** - Change `NvdDownloader.semaphore` from `@property` to `@cached_property` - Share a single `asyncio.Semaphore(self.args.max_concurrency)` across all page fetches for the life of the runner - **Transient failure retrying** - Extend `fetch_page` retry handling beyond HTTP `429` - Retry `aiohttp.ClientError` and `asyncio.TimeoutError` with the existing backoff pattern - Log each transient retry at warning level with the exception, attempt, and backoff - Preserve existing `429` handling and success-path behavior - **Bounded request lifetime** - Add an explicit `aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=300)` to the session in `fetch_window` - Ensure hung or stalled requests fail into the retry path instead of blocking indefinitely ```python @cached_property def semaphore(self): return asyncio.Semaphore(self.args.max_concurrency) async def fetch_page(self, session, start_date, end_date, start_index): for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1): try: async with self.semaphore: async with session.get(url) as resp: if resp.status == 429: ... resp.raise_for_status() return ..., await resp.json() except (aiohttp.ClientError, asyncio.TimeoutError) as e: ... ```

signals.text: PR #45752 ("Change CommandParser::parse to return StatusOr") was based on `main` before the CVE-2026-47220 fix (commit `4a70d8d594`) landed. The CVE fix added null guards to `RequestedServerNameFormatter::getHostFromHeaders()` for `Host()` and `EnvoyOriginalHost()` headers. The PR's code removed those guards, causing runtime crashes in `compile_time_options` CI (which enables UHV and exercises more header edge cases). ## Changes - **API change** (`envoy/formatter/substitution_formatter.h`): `CommandParser::parse` virtual method now returns `absl::StatusOr<FormatterProviderPtr>` instead of `FormatterProviderPtr` - **Formatter implementations** (`source/common/formatter/`, `source/extensions/formatter/`): All `parse` overrides updated to return `absl::StatusOr<FormatterProviderPtr>` - **Extension formatters**: `cel`, `dynamic_modules`, `file_content`, `generic_secret`, `metadata`, `req_without_query`, `xfcc_value`, DNS filter access log — all updated - **CVE fix preserved**: `getHostFromHeaders()` retains null checks from the CVE-2026-47220 fix: ```cpp // Safe version (preserved from CVE fix): case HostOnly: { if (auto host = headers->Host(); host != nullptr) { result = host->value().getStringView(); } break; } case OriginalHostOrHost: { if (auto orig = headers->EnvoyOriginalHost(); orig != nullptr) { result = orig->value().getStringView(); } else if (auto host = headers->Host(); host != nullptr) { result = host->value().getStringView(); } break; } ``` - **Tests**: CVE regression tests (`stream_info_no_requested_name_no_headers`) preserved alongside updated StatusOr call sites

signals.title: tsan: investigate and fix TSAN failure for createJsonFormatter StatusOr change
signals.text: ## Context PR #45831 changes `SubstitutionFormatStringUtils::createJsonFormatter` return type from `FormatterPtr` to `absl::StatusOr<FormatterPtr>`, and the TSAN CI job failed during that run (exit code 3 — test failure, not build failure). ## Investigation The session exhausted quota before a conclusive root cause was identified or a code fix implemented. Key findings from the analysis: - **CI artifacts were inaccessible**: Job 83338832915 logs only showed post-processing tail; the `ci-report-tsan.json` artifact contained only disk usage stats; the EngFlow BES invocation URL was not reachable externally. - **Two concurrent changes are in scope**: The PR's formatter `StatusOr` changes *and* the TLS `read_disabled_` logic introduced in main at `df2c77d` (`tls: fix connection close detection while handshake is waiting`), which ships a new `AsyncCertSelectionCancellationObservedOnDownstreamClose` integration test. - **ASAN passed / TSAN failed**: This is characteristic of a data race, not a memory safety issue — pointing away from the formatter change itself. - **Prime suspect**: `CancellableSelectionHandle` destructor in `async_cert_selector.h` holds an `Event::TimerPtr` and `CertificateSelectionCallbackPtr`; if destroyed off the dispatcher thread (e.g., when the downstream connection closes and tears down `SslExtendedSocketInfoImpl`), TSAN would flag it as a data race. ## Status ⚠️ **Incomplete** — no code changes were committed. Further work is needed to: 1. Retrieve the actual TSAN report (stack traces) from a fresh CI run 2. Confirm the `CancellableSelectionHandle` destruction threading hypothesis 3. Implement the fix (likely ensuring cert-selector handle destruction is posted back to the dispatcher thread, or guarding access with appropriate synchronization)

signals.title: test: fix flaky xds_failover StartupPrimaryNotResponding for GoogleGrpc TRANSIENT_FAILURE
signals.text: `XdsFailoverAdsIntegrationTest.StartupPrimaryNotResponding/15` (IPv6, GoogleGrpc, UnifiedDelta) fails intermittently under ASAN due to a race between gRPC's real-time channel backoff and Envoy's simulated-time retry timer. ## Root cause After the first `primaryConnectionFailure()` closes the TCP connection, the gRPC channel enters `TRANSIENT_FAILURE` with a ~1s real-time backoff. `waitForPrimaryXdsRetryTimer()` advances **simulated** time, firing Envoy's retry timer before that real-time backoff expires. The gRPC library immediately rejects the `establishNewStream()` attempt (no TCP connection made), which counts as the 2nd consecutive failure and triggers failover. The test's second `primaryConnectionFailure()` then waits 30s (ASAN `DefaultTimeout`) for a primary TCP connection that never arrives — Envoy has already switched to failover — hitting the `RELEASE_ASSERT`. This race is timing-sensitive: for IPv4 the gRPC library fast-retries before `onEstablishmentFailure` fires (channel stays in `CONNECTING`), so the race doesn't manifest there. ## Fix In `StartupPrimaryNotResponding`, before the second `primaryConnectionFailure()` call, poll (real-time only, **no** simulated clock advancement) for `cds.update_failure ≥ 2` within `200×TIMEOUT_FACTOR` ms. If the counter reaches 2, the 2nd failure already occurred via `TRANSIENT_FAILURE` and the explicit TCP-close step is skipped: ```cpp bool second_failure_via_transient_failure = false; if (clientType() == Grpc::ClientType::GoogleGrpc) { const auto deadline = absl::Now() + absl::Milliseconds(200 * TIMEOUT_FACTOR); constexpr absl::Duration kPollInterval = absl::Milliseconds(5); while (absl::Now() < deadline) { const auto counter = TestUtility::findCounter( test_server_->statStore(), "cluster_manager.cds.update_failure"); if (counter != nullptr && counter->value() >= 2) { second_failure_via_transient_failure = true; break; } absl::SleepFor(kPollInterval); } } if (!second_failure_via_transient_failure) { primaryConnectionFailure(); ASSERT_TRUE(xds_connection_->waitForDisconnect()); } ``` Polling uses real time (not `advanceTimeWait`) to avoid firing additional simulated timers that could interfere with test state. The `200×TIMEOUT_FACTOR` window is well above the typical <60ms propagation latency for the gRPC completion queue → Envoy main thread path. ## Files changed - **`test/extensions/config_subscription/grpc/xds_failover_integration_test.cc`** — TRANSIENT_FAILURE detection + `absl/time` includes - **`test/extensions/config_subscription/grpc/BUILD`** — added `@abseil-cpp//absl/time` dep

signals.title: Recycles slices allocated by OwnedImpl back to the thread-local freelist
signals.text: This change allows mutable slices of default size (16KB) to be recycled back to the thread-local freelist when they are drained and destroyed, rather than being deleted. This reduces memory allocation frequency for steady-state read operations. We introduce a static `recycle` method to `OwnedImplReservationSlicesOwnerMultiple` and call it from `Slice` destructor. To resolve circular dependency, the `Slice` destructor is declared in the class and defined inline at the end of the header. We also make `Slice` a friend of `OwnedImpl` to allow access to the private nested class. Added unit tests in `buffer_test.cc` to verify: - Successful recycling and reuse of default-sized slices. - Non-default-sized slices are not recycled. The freelist size is expanded slightly to reduce freelist thrashing when multiple connections are fetching and freeing slices. This change was entirely generated by the Gemini AI model. signals.title: composite: fail over to the next sub-cluster when a sub-cluster has no hosts
signals.text: ## Commit Message composite: fail over to the next sub-cluster when a sub-cluster has no hosts The composite cluster failed a request with 503 no_healthy_upstream when the sub-cluster mapped to the current attempt had no host available, for example because DNS resolution returned an empty endpoint list or because all of its hosts had been ejected. Host selection now advances to the following sub-clusters in the configured list within the same attempt, and only fails when none of them can provide a host. Guarded by `envoy.reloadable_features.composite_cluster_skip_clusters_without_hosts`. ## Additional Description ### Documented behavior vs. actual behavior The `composite_cluster` [docs](https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/intro/arch_overview/upstream/composite_cluster) stated: > *"If a selected sub-cluster has no healthy hosts available, the request will fail according to that sub-cluster's load balancing behavior, **potentially triggering another retry attempt if configured**."* In practice that retry path was unreachable: `no_healthy_upstream` is a routing-level rejection raised before any upstream connection attempt, and no `retry_on` condition covers it. A composite cluster whose first sub-cluster had zero endpoints failed with `503 no_healthy_upstream` regardless of the retry policy, so per-request failover did not work at all in that scenario. ### Change from the previous revision of this PR The first revision of this PR added a core `no-healthy-upstream` retry condition (`RETRY_ON_NO_HEALTHY_UPSTREAM`) plus a hook in `Filter::createConnPoolOrHandleFailure()`. Per review feedback from @wbpcode and @agrawroh, that a core feature serving one extension is the wrong layer, and that the composite cluster should pick a sub-cluster that has healthy hosts itself. The previous approach has been fully reverted and the fix now lives entirely in the extension. Reverted back to `main`: `envoy/router/router.h`, `source/common/http/headers.h`, `source/common/router/retry_state_impl.{h,cc}`, `source/common/router/router.cc`, `test/common/router/{router_test,retry_state_impl_test}.cc`, `test/mocks/router/mocks.{h,cc}`, `api/envoy/config/route/v3/route_components.proto`, `docs/root/configuration/http/http_filters/router_filter.rst`. ### Fix `CompositeClusterLoadBalancer::chooseHost()` still maps the attempt count to a starting cluster index, but host selection now runs through a new `selectHostWithFailover()` helper that walks forward from that index: * A sub-cluster is skipped when it is not present in the cluster manager, or when its load balancer returns no host. * Selection returns immediately when a host is selected, or when the sub-cluster started asynchronous host selection (`HostSelectionResponse::cancelable` set), so an in-flight async selection is not abandoned or duplicated. * When no sub-cluster can provide a host, the `details` and `failure_status` of the last sub-cluster tried are propagated, so the resulting local reply keeps the same diagnostics as before. Availability is determined by asking the sub-cluster's load balancer rather than by inspecting its priority set, so nested composite/aggregate sub-clusters, `CLUSTER_PROVIDED` sub-clusters, panic mode and override-host behavior all keep working. When a sub-cluster can serve the attempt, its load balancer is the only one invoked, so there are no wasted host selections on the happy path. ### Behavior notes * Selection remains driven by the attempt count: an attempt that failed over to a later sub-cluster does not shift the mapping of subsequent attempts. With `[primary, secondary, fallback]` and an empty `primary`, attempt 1 uses `secondary` and attempt 2 also maps to `secondary`. This is documented in the arch overview. If reviewers prefer that a failover also advance the following attempts, that can be done by recording the used index in filter state — happy to add it here or as a follow-up. * `peekAnotherHost()` and `selectExistingConnection()` keep the plain attempt mapping. Every in-tree `selectExistingConnection()` implementation returns `nullopt`, so there is no practical mismatch, and prefetching does not need the failover. ### Minimal reproduction A minimal Docker Compose reproduction of the original bug is available at: https://github.com/JonSchaeffer/playground/tree/main/envoy/composite-bug-minimal-repro ## Risk Level Low — the change is scoped to the composite cluster extension, and it is behind a reloadable runtime guard. ## Testing * Unit tests in `test/extensions/clusters/composite/cluster_test.cc`: failover when the selected sub-cluster has no host, failover when the selected sub-cluster is missing from the cluster manager, no host plus preserved failure details when no sub-cluster can serve the request, asynchronous host selection returned without trying other sub-clusters, and legacy behavior with the runtime guard disabled. * Integration tests in `test/extensions/clusters/composite/cluster_integration_test.cc`: failover with `num_retries: 0` (proving no retry is involved), failover across two consecutive sub-clusters without endpoints, `503` when no sub-cluster has endpoints, and `503` with the runtime guard disabled. The two `no-healthy-upstream` retry tests from the previous revision were removed. * Format and spelling checks: `bazel run //tools/code_format:check_format` and `bazel run //tools/spelling:check_spelling_pedantic` both pass. ## Docs Changes * `docs/root/intro/arch_overview/upstream/composite_cluster.rst`: new "Hosts availability" section, updated the sub-cluster health / deterministic routing considerations, and documented the runtime guard and the attempt-progression caveat. * `api/envoy/extensions/clusters/composite/v3/cluster.proto`: comment-only update describing the failover. No field or type changes. ## Release Notes `changelogs/current/bug_fixes/composite_cluster__skip-clusters-without-hosts.rst`. ## Runtime guard `envoy.reloadable_features.composite_cluster_skip_clusters_without_hosts` (enabled by default). Setting it to `false` restores the previous behavior of failing the attempt when the sub-cluster mapped to that attempt has no host available. --- > **Note:** This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The author has reviewed and > understands all changes.

signals.title: ci/wasm: Re-enable wasmtime engine tests with hermetic cmake
signals.text: The wasmtime phase of `compile_time_options` has been silently skipped due to an inverted bash check in `ci/do_ci.sh`. Re-enabling it ([failing run](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/actions/runs/28031800806/job/82974411548)) surfaces two breakages that accumulated in the meantime. This PR flips the check and fixes both. ### Re-enable wasmtime tests - `ci/do_ci.sh`: `-z` → `-n` on `ENVOY_SKIP_CTO_WASMTIME`, so the wasmtime phase runs unless explicitly skipped (same flip as on the target branch; will dedupe on merge). ### Hermetic cmake for the wasmtime-c-api-impl build script The crate's `build.rs` spawns `cmake` to install headers, which doesn't exist on the RBE image. Instead of adding cmake to the image, this wires in rules_foreign_cc's prebuilt hermetic cmake toolchain: - New `bazel/wasmtime_c_api_impl.patch` makes `build.rs` honor a `$CMAKE` env var: ```rust let cmake_bin = env::var("CMAKE").unwrap_or_else(|_| "cmake".to_string()); ``` - `bazel/proxy_wasm_cpp_host.patch` extended to apply that patch to the `cu__wasmtime-c-api-impl-45.0.2` crate repo and wire the toolchain into its `cargo_build_script`: ```python build_script_env = {"CMAKE": "$${pwd}/$(CMAKE)"}, toolchains = ["@rules_foreign_cc//toolchains:current_cmake_toolchain"], ``` The toolchain expands `$(CMAKE)` to the exec-root-relative binary path and stages cmake as an action input; rules_rust substitutes `${pwd}` at runtime. - Existing patch sections gained `diff --git` headers — Bazel's patcher mis-applies multi-file unified diffs without them (hunks silently accumulate onto the last-named file). ### Rust 1.88.0 → 1.93.0 The current proxy_wasm_cpp_host pin pulls wasmtime 45.0.2 crates with `rust-version = "1.93.0"`; `wasmtime_environ` fails on 1.88 (E0658 on `fmt::from_fn`). Bumped `rust_register_toolchains` in `bazel/dependency_imports.bzl`. The only other in-repo Rust consumers (dynamic modules SDK/builtin extensions) build cleanly on 1.93. --- 🤖 This PR was created with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot coding agent).

signals.title: docs/bazel: research on keeping hermetic LLVM toolchain working on macOS with LLVM 22
signals.text: macOS CI fails on the LLVM 22 bump (#46297) with the hermetic `toolchains_llvm` toolchain, while the host compiler works. This adds `bazel/llvm-22-macos-hermetic-toolchain.md` with the research requested to establish what is required to keep the hermetic toolchain working. ## Key findings - **Root cause**: `toolchains_llvm` ≤ v1.7.0 on macOS compiles with the hermetic toolchain's bundled libc++ headers but links `-lc++ -lc++abi` from the Xcode SDK sysroot. LLVM 21 moved libc++ hashing out of line (new exported symbol `std::__1::__hash_memory`), so any hermetic LLVM ≥ 21 hits the header/library ABI mismatch: ``` ld64.lld: error: undefined symbol: std::__1::__hash_memory(void const*, unsigned long) >>> referenced by .../abseil-cpp/absl/strings/_objs/cord/cord_analysis.o ``` LLVM 18.1.8 only worked because the version skew was latent. - **Host compiler works** because Apple clang uses the SDK's libc++ headers *and* library — a consistent pair. - **Out-of-band downloads (`extra_llvm_distributions`) are a red herring** — the archive downloads and compiles fine; failure is at link. - **Fixed upstream** in `toolchains_llvm` v1.8.0 (commit `68822c1`, PR bazel-contrib/toolchains_llvm#748, issue #666): macOS now uses the SDK's libc++ end to end, matching host-compiler behavior. ## Options documented - **A (recommended)**: upgrade to toolchains_llvm v1.8.0 — drop `toolchains_llvm_stdc++.patch` (fixed upstream), rebase the toolshed `cxx_cross_lib` patch (needs a new `envoy_toolshed` release; `configure.bzl` was heavily reworked), handle new transitive deps (`helly25_bzl`, `bazel_features` 1.48.1, `rules_cc` 0.2.19), keep `extra_llvm_distributions` for 22.1.8 (v1.8.0's table stops at 22.1.7). - **B**: backport the darwin fix as an extra patch on v1.7.0 (small, but temporary; the upstream commit doesn't apply cleanly). - **C (not recommended)**: per-platform version pinning, static hermetic libc++, or host compiler on macOS. Also documents the consequence: post-fix, macOS builds against the SDK's libc++ (bounded by pinned `XCODE_VERSION`), with only the compiler coming from LLVM 22 — same baseline as the host compiler today. Documentation-only change. Created with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot task agent).

signals.title: bazel: make toolchains_llvm date-macro redaction configurable via exec-config feature flag
signals.text: `toolchains_llvm` v1.8 unconditionally injects `-imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h` into every C/C++ compile via `unfiltered_compile_flags`. The execroot-relative path resolves fine for normal Bazel `cc` actions but fails in Cargo build-script `cc` invocations (e.g. `ring`) whose working directory isn't the Bazel execroot: ``` cargo:warning=<built-in>:1:19: fatal error: 'external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h' file not found ``` **Design B** — keep redaction ON in target-config compiles (no cache churn), drop it only in exec-config compiles. Bazel resets `--features` → `--host_features` in the exec configuration, so `--host_features=no-redact-dates` naturally scopes the opt-out to build-script `cc` calls without touching target-config action keys. ## Changes - **`bazel/foreign_cc/toolchains_llvm_configurable_redacted_dates.patch`** — patch against pinned `toolchains_llvm` v1.8.0: - Adds `no_redact_dates` `config_setting` to `toolchain/config/BUILD.bazel` matching `values = {"features": "no-redact-dates"}` (same style as existing `use_asan`/`use_ubsan`/`use_tsan`) - Removes the `-Wno-builtin-macro-redefined`/`-imacros`/`redacted_dates_path` lines from the baked `unfiltered_compile_flags` list and builds `redact_dates_flags = select({no_redact_dates: [], default: [redaction flags]})` - Concatenates via `+` at the final `unix_cc_toolchain_config(...)` call site — required because Starlark disallows `list.extend(select(...))`; the earlier `.extend()` calls on `unfiltered_compile_flags` all precede this and remain unaffected - **`bazel/repositories.bzl`** — appends the new patch to `_toolchains_llvm()`'s `patches` list - **`.bazelrc`** — adds `common:clang-common --host_features=no-redact-dates` alongside the existing `compiler-rt=false`/`libunwind=false` lines, scoping the opt-out to exec-config compiles for all clang builds (including RBE `release.test_only`)

signals.title: bazel: fix `ring` build-script resolution of `redacted_dates.h`
signals.text: `ring`'s `cargo_build_script` inherits the LLVM toolchain's `-imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h` via `rules_rust`'s cc-toolchain wiring, but that execroot-relative path does not resolve from the build script's default run directory. This keeps date redaction fully enabled and instead makes the existing toolchain path resolvable for `ring` only. - **Trace** - `toolchains_llvm` bakes `-Wno-builtin-macro-redefined -imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h` into `unfiltered_compile_flags`. - `rules_rust`'s `cargo_build_script` derives `CC`/`CFLAGS`/`CXXFLAGS` from the cc toolchain and forwards them to `cc-rs`. - As seen in the failing `CargoBuildScriptRun`, `ring` receives: ```text CC=external/llvm_toolchain/bin/cc_wrapper.sh CFLAGS=... -imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h ``` - `redacted_dates.h` is generated in the `@llvm_toolchain` repo and exists in the execroot at `external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h`. - **Change** - Add a crate-universe annotation for `ring` in `/home/runner/work/envoy/envoy/bazel/dependency_imports.bzl`. - Declare `@llvm_toolchain//:redacted_dates.h` as build-script data. - Set the build script `rundir` to `.` so `ring` runs from the execroot, matching the toolchain's relative path. - Regenerate `/home/runner/work/envoy/envoy/Cargo.Bazel.lock` to apply the annotation to `ring`'s generated `cargo_build_script`. - **Why this scope** - No `toolchains_llvm` patch. - No `.bazelrc` / `--host_features` change. - No change to redaction semantics, no absolute paths, no toolchain-wide action rekeying. - Only the affected crate build-script action is adjusted. - **Generated shape** ```starlark "ring": [crate.annotation( build_script_data = ["@llvm_toolchain//:redacted_dates.h"], build_script_rundir = ".", )] ``` - **Problem-statement evidence** - Target/host C++ compile redaction remains intact: representative `CppCompile` `aquery` output is unchanged before/after, including the same `ActionKey` and the same `-imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h`. - The `ring` fix is localized: its `CargoBuildScriptRun` still carries the same redaction flags; the relevant delta is `--rundir=.` plus the declared header input. - A probe compiled with the LLVM toolchain flags still emits `redacted` for date/time macros rather than real datestamps. - The previously failing `@envoy_rust_crate_index__ring-0.17.14//:_bs` build now succeeds with the toolchain configuration unchanged. - **AI assist** - Copilot assisted with investigation and patch preparation; the change and evidence were reviewed before submission.

signals.title: Split reverse connection cluster tests into smaller gcc-friendly translation units
signals.text: `reverse_connection_cluster_test.cc` had grown into a single large TU that could time out under gcc on constrained CI workers. This change keeps the test coverage and behavior intact while reducing per-TU compile cost by partitioning the test file into smaller units. - **Shared test scaffold** - Extract the common reverse-connection test infrastructure into `reverse_connection_cluster_test_base.h`. - Move the shared helper and fixtures there: - `TestLoadBalancerContext` - `ReverseConnectionClusterTest` - `UpstreamReverseConnectionAddressTest` - Keep fixture method definitions header-inline so each split TU reuses the same setup without introducing new linkage structure. - **Split by concern** - Replace the monolithic test source with focused TUs: - `reverse_connection_cluster_config_test.cc` - `reverse_connection_cluster_lb_test.cc` - `reverse_connection_cluster_formatter_test.cc` - `reverse_connection_cluster_address_test.cc` - Preserve the existing test cases and assertions; this is a mechanical relocation only. - **Build graph update** - Add a shared `envoy_cc_test_library` for the common header and shared deps. - Replace the single `envoy_cc_test` with one test target per split source. - Keep per-file extras local to the TUs that need them (for example formatter-related stream info mocks and `absl::StrCat`). Example of the new structure: ```starlark envoy_cc_test_library( name = "reverse_connection_cluster_test_base", hdrs = ["reverse_connection_cluster_test_base.h"], deps = [...], ) envoy_cc_test( name = "reverse_connection_cluster_lb_test", srcs = ["reverse_connection_cluster_lb_test.cc"], deps = [":reverse_connection_cluster_test_base"], ) ```

signals.title: ci: auto-label PRs opened against release/v* branches
signals.text: PRs opened against `release/v*` branches should automatically receive `backport` and `changelog-required` labels, with opt-out via `changelog-not-required`. This hooks into the existing `Request` pipeline rather than adding a new `pull_request_target` workflow. ## Changes to `_request.yml` - **`incoming` job — new `Compute labels` step + `labels` output** - Uses the already-pinned `envoyproxy/toolshed/actions/jq` to evaluate target branch and existing PR labels - Emits a compact JSON array (`["backport","changelog-required"]`, `["backport"]`, or `[]`) - `[]` for any non-`release/v*` target; no write permissions here - **New `label` job** (`needs: incoming`) - Only job with `permissions: pull-requests: write`; performs no checkout - Gated on `pull_request_target` + `action == 'opened'` + non-empty `labels` output - Belt-and-suspenders allowlist in the script (`{'backport', 'changelog-required'}`) rejects anything `incoming` might emit outside these two names - Uses `actions/github-script` (already used in this repo, same pinned SHA) to call `addLabels`; errors are caught and surfaced as warnings rather than hard failures ```yaml label: if: >- ${{ (github.repository == 'envoyproxy/envoy' || vars.ENVOY_CI) && github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.action == 'opened' && needs.incoming.outputs.labels != '[]' }} needs: incoming permissions: pull-requests: write steps: - uses: actions/github-script@... with: script: | const ALLOWLIST = new Set(['backport', 'changelog-required']); const labels = JSON.parse('...').filter(l => ALLOWLIST.has(l)); await github.rest.issues.addLabels({ ..., labels }); ``` The `incoming` job carries no write credentials; creds are confined to `label`. Structure is a thin wrapper ready to migrate to a `envoyproxy/toolshed` action later.

signals.title: Use PassthroughState pointer value as thread local storage key for peer metadata exchange
signals.text: Commit Message: This pull request introduces a new mechanism for Istio peer_metadata filters communicating across an internal socket/listener to exchange peer metadata information through thread local storage. The previous implementation would do inject peer metadata into the data stream directly, but that does not work when internal transport socket wraps a PROXY or TLS socket because those aren't prepared to use handle the arbitrary data injected into the data stream. To fix that problem we tried to use thread local storage instead of injecting data into the data stream and used downstream connection ID as a shared key in the thread local storage that both filters are aware of, but that approach does not work well when multiple requests are multiplexed over the same downstream HTTP2 connection - they would share the same downstream connection ID and will use the same key for thread local storage, even if the destinations are different. The new implementation in this PR uses thread local storage, just like the approach above, but instead of using downstream connection ID it uses PassthroughState pointer value as a key. PassthroughState pointer is basically allocated per upstream connection, so that addresses the issue with multiplexed requests - as we get a unique key per upstream connection after endpoint selection and multiplexing decisions have been made already. Additional Description: Risk Level: low - feature is specific to Istio and does not touch core Envoy, and it's disabled by default. Testing: integration tests Docs Changes: n/a Release Notes: n/a Platform Specific Features: n/a

signals.title: bazel(workspace): switch protobuf/protoc to canonical prebuilt toolchain path
signals.text: Envoy’s WORKSPACE path was still using a custom prebuilt-protoc mechanism (`//:protoc` override patch + `com_google_protobuf_protoc_*` repos). This change moves WORKSPACE mode to protobuf’s canonical prebuilt toolchain flow and removes Envoy-specific prebuilt-protoc repo plumbing, without touching bzlmod/MODULE behavior. - **WORKSPACE toolchain wiring** - Added `bazel/protobuf_toolchains.bzl` and invoked it from `WORKSPACE` after `com_google_protobuf` is available. - Instantiates `@prebuilt_protoc.<platform>` repos from protobuf’s `PROTOBUF_PLATFORMS` via `prebuilt_protoc_repo`. - Registers protobuf prebuilt toolchains: - `@com_google_protobuf//bazel/private/oss/toolchains/prebuilt:all` - Enabled workspace flag in `.bazelrc`: - `--@com_google_protobuf//bazel/flags:prefer_prebuilt_protoc=true` - **Remove Envoy home-grown prebuilt-protoc machinery** - Dropped `PROTOC_VERSIONS` and `_compiled_protoc_deps` from `bazel/repository_locations.bzl`. - Removed creation of `com_google_protobuf_protoc_*` repos from `bazel/repositories.bzl`. - Removed corresponding `com_google_protobuf_protoc_*` metadata from `bazel/deps.yaml`. - Removed protobuf patch hunk that rewired `//:protoc` to Envoy-managed prebuilt repos. - **Patch updates retained for WORKSPACE correctness** - Kept unrelated/required protobuf patch hunks (`cpp_opts`, zlib label mapping). - Added `bazel/protobuf_prebuilt_tool_integrity.patch` so WORKSPACE tarball builds have complete v35.1 prebuilt protoc integrity entries across protobuf’s platform set. - **Direct protoc invocation audit + handling** - Added Envoy-owned stable shim target `//bazel:protoc` for direct label-style consumers that can use file-backed tool selection. - Repointed `bazel/envoy_build_system.bzl` descriptor genrule path to `@envoy//bazel:protoc`. - Kept executable-attr direct consumers (`tools/api_proto_plugin/plugin.bzl`, `api/bazel/cc_proto_descriptor_library/builddefs.bzl`) on `@com_google_protobuf//:protoc` to preserve executable-target semantics and avoid breakage. ```starlark # bazel/BUILD alias( name = "protoc", actual = select({ ":linux_x86_64": "@prebuilt_protoc.linux_x86_64//:bin/protoc", ":darwin_arm64": "@prebuilt_protoc.osx_aarch_64//:bin/protoc", ":windows_x86_64": "@prebuilt_protoc.win64//:bin/protoc.exe", "//conditions:default": "@com_google_protobuf//:protoc", }), ) ```

signals.title: tls_inspector: add optional protocol parameter to JA4Fingerprinter::create
signals.text: ## Summary Per the [JA4 spec](https://github.com/FoxIO-LLC/ja4/blob/main/technical_details/JA4.md), the first character of a JA4 fingerprint identifies the transport carrying the handshake: `t` for TLS, `q` for QUIC, `d` for DTLS. Envoy's implementation currently hard-codes `t` with a comment noting that only TLS is handled. This change adds a public `JA4Fingerprinter::Protocol` enum and a defaulted second argument to `JA4Fingerprinter::create` so callers can select the transport they observed. - The default (`Protocol::TLS`) preserves the exact prior behavior of every existing caller, including the built-in TLS inspector listener filter — its call site is deliberately left byte-identical, since that filter only sees stream TLS handshakes today and has no new information to convey. - A downstream deployment that terminates QUIC (or a future in-tree QUIC listener filter that wants JA4) can now pass `Protocol::QUIC` and produce spec-conformant `q...` fingerprints without touching the JA4 library. ## Design notes - `Protocol` is nested inside `JA4Fingerprinter` and scoped `enum class : char`. This is a static utility class, so nesting keeps the enum tightly bound to its only consumer. - Mapping happens through a small `switch` in an anonymous namespace rather than treating the enum value as a raw `char`. That's easier to read and makes any future non-single-character protocol identifier a compile-time obligation rather than an implicit reinterpretation. ## Test plan - [x] Added `TEST(JA4Fingerprinter, ProtocolParameterControlsFirstCharacter)` in `ja4_fingerprint_test.cc` that: - Verifies the no-arg `create(&hello)` is byte-identical to `create(&hello, Protocol::TLS)`. - Verifies `Protocol::QUIC` and `Protocol::DTLS` produce fingerprints starting with `q` and `d` respectively. - Verifies the protocol argument affects **only** the first character; all other bytes of the fingerprint match across protocol choices. - [x] `bazel test //test/extensions/filters/listener/tls_inspector:ja4_fingerprint_test` passes locally. - [x] `git diff origin/main -- source/extensions/filters/listener/tls_inspector/tls_inspector.cc` is empty — no existing call site changed. ## Notes - The pinned expected hashes in `tls_inspector_ja4_test.cc` were computed under the current `t`-only default; since the default is preserved they remain valid without modification. - This change was drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by the author.

In doing this, I refactored some of the existing exporter instantiation code in opentelemetry_tracer_impl.cc to make it more efficient, logically grouped, and thread safe. #### Features Added * Added exporter field to opentelemetry.proto and wrapped exporter, grpc_service, and http_service fields in a oneof block to enforce early validation, and make the API contract more clear. * Added OpenTelemetryTraceExporterFactory to trace_exporter.h to allow custom exporters to be created and registered. * Added code to opentelemetry_tracer_impl.cc to resolve custom exporter factories and unpack custom config in the main thread, and instantiate the custom exporter on each worker thread. #### Refactored Code * Moved gRPC client factory creation from worker thread to main thread, so that an exception won’t be thrown in the worker thread if the creation fails. * Removed the need to make a deep copy when capturing opentelemetry_config in the worker thread lambda by extracting the relevant fields, and capturing shared pointers to those fields. * Added an early return statement to flushSpans() in tracer.cc if exporter_ is nullptr, and added code to increment tracing_stats_.spans_dropped_. * Replaced raw reference to factory_context with a shared pointer in worker thread lambda to prevent any use-after-free issues, and replaced the passed-in factory_context’s validation visitor with a nullValidationVisitor to prevent any worker threads from mutating the main thread’s descriptions_ hash set, which is not thread safe. ### Additional Description AI was used to generate the code and tests in this PR. signals.title: oauth2: configurable audience and key_id in private_key_jwt client assertion
signals.text: <!-- !!!ATTENTION!!! If you are fixing **any** crash or **any** potential security issue, **do not open a pull request**. Instead, please [open a GitHub Security Advisory](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/new) (preferred). Alternatively, you may email envoy-security@googlegroups.com. Thank you in advance for helping to keep Envoy secure. !!!ATTENTION!!! For an explanation of how to fill out the fields, please see the relevant section in [PULL_REQUESTS.md](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/blob/main/PULL_REQUESTS.md) !!!ATTENTION!!! Please check the [use of generative AI policy](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L41). You may use generative AI only if you fully understand the code. You need to disclose this usage in the PR description to ensure transparency. --> Commit Message: oauth2: configurable audience and key_id in private_key_jwt client assertion Adds two optional fields to `PrivateKeyJwtConfig` so the JWT client assertion can satisfy identity providers that reject the values Envoy currently emits: * `assertion_audience` sets the `aud` claim of the client assertion. OIDC Core Section 9 recommends the token endpoint URL, but RFC 9126 Section 2.1 and FAPI 2.0 recommend the authorization server's issuer identifier, and some providers require it. When unset, the `aud` claim remains the configured `token_endpoint` URI. * `key_id` sets the `kid` JOSE header of the assertion per RFC 7515 Section 4.1.4, which providers use to select the correct verification key when a client has more than one key registered. When unset, no `kid` header is emitted. Both fields are opt-in and default to the previous behavior, so existing configurations are unaffected. Additional Description: Private key JWT client authentication was requested in #40127 and implemented in #44005. When testing that support against ID-Porten (Norway's public sector IDP for norwegian citizens), token requests were rejected for two reasons: the provider expects its issuer identifier as the assertion audience rather than the token endpoint URL, and it requires a `kid` header to select the verification key among the several keys registered for the client. Both are permitted by the relevant specifications, but Envoy currently derives the `aud` claim from `token_endpoint` with no way to override it, and never emits a `kid` header at all, so the feature cannot be used with providers of this kind. Rather than changing the defaults, both values are exposed as optional fields so existing deployments keep working unchanged. This PR was developed with AI assistance. I have reviewed and fully understand all of the code being submitted. Risk Level: Low (small optional feature; new fields are opt-in and defaults preserve existing behavior) Testing: Unit tests. Extended `client_assertion_test` to cover the `kid` header being present when configured and absent when not; extended `filter_test` to cover the audience defaulting to the token endpoint URI, an explicitly configured audience, and decoding the generated assertion to assert the resulting `aud` claim; extended `config_test` to cover loading a configuration that sets the new fields. Docs Changes: API documentation inline with the proto fields in `api/envoy/extensions/filters/http/oauth2/v3/oauth.proto`, including references to the relevant specs and the default behavior when each field is unset. No changes to docs/root were needed. Release Notes: Added `changelogs/current/new_features/oauth2__assertion-audience-and-key-id.rst`. Platform Specific Features: N/A Runtime guard: N/A. Both fields are optional and default to the existing behavior, so there is no user-visible behavioral change for configurations that do not set them. Fixes #Issue: N/A — follow-up to #40127 / #44005, which are already closed. API Considerations(https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/blob/main/api/review_checklist.md): * Feature enablement: both fields are opt-in. Unset `assertion_audience` preserves the current `aud` value (the `token_endpoint` URI) and unset `key_id` omits the `kid` header entirely, so no existing user is affected without a config change. * WKT wrapping: both are `string`, where empty unambiguously means "unset"; there is no plausible future default that would require a wrapper type. * Validation: no protoc-gen-validate rules are added. Both are optional free-form identifiers whose valid values are defined by the identity provider (`aud` may be any string per RFC 7519, and `kid` any string per RFC 7515), so constraining them in the API would risk rejecting legitimate provider configurations. cc @kanurag94

signals.title: quic: support P-384 and P-521 EC certificates
signals.text: Fixes: https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/issues/46694 #### Description QUIC listeners were restricted to the P-256 EC curve by default, preventing the use of P-384 and P-521 EC certificates. ### Changes This change enables support for P-384 and P-521 EC curves for QUIC listeners. ### Testing Could recreate the issue same as described in https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/issues/46694. Tested with the following settings: <details> <summary>envoy config</summary> ``` static_resources: listeners: # TCP listener for HTTPS / HTTP2. - name: http2_listener address: socket_address: address: 0.0.0.0 port_value: 10000 protocol: TCP filter_chains: - transport_socket: name: envoy.transport_sockets.tls typed_config: "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.transport_sockets.tls.v3.DownstreamTlsContext common_tls_context: alpn_protocols: - h2 - http/1.1 tls_certificates: - certificate_chain: filename: certs/domain1.crt.pem private_key: filename: certs/domain1.key.pem filters: - name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager typed_config: "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager codec_type: HTTP2 stat_prefix: ingress_http route_config: name: local_route virtual_hosts: - name: app domains: - "*" # Tell the browser that HTTP/3 is available. response_headers_to_add: - header: key: alt-svc value: 'h3=":10000"; ma=86400' routes: - match: prefix: "/" route: cluster: proxy-domain1 http_filters: - name: envoy.filters.http.router typed_config: "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.router.v3.Router # UDP listener for QUIC / HTTP3. - name: http3_listener address: socket_address: address: 0.0.0.0 port_value: 10000 protocol: UDP udp_listener_config: quic_options: {} filter_chains: - filters: - name: signals.title: ratelimit: preserve one token for local cluster shares
signals.text: **Commit Message:** `ratelimit: preserve one token for local cluster shares` When `local_cluster_rate_limit` is configured, a request that normally consumes one token consumes one token per local cluster member. If the member count exceeds `max_tokens`, the request costs more than the bucket can hold, so every matching request is rejected. This PR adds a runtime guard for the fix. The guard is off by default, so current behavior does not change until operators enable it. When enabled, the effective maximum per Envoy for a bucket with `max_tokens > 0` is `max(floor(max_tokens / membership), 1)`. A bucket with `max_tokens: 0` continues to reject every request. **Additional Description:** PR #35207 added the atomic token bucket and moved local-cluster sharing from refill-time rounding to request-cost scaling. That change preserved normal shares but introduced a zero-capacity case when the membership share became smaller than `1 / max_tokens`. PR #38197 later removed the previous timer-based implementation and its rollback flag. There is an unavoidable tradeoff when `membership > max_tokens` because independent Envoys cannot divide fewer than one token evenly: - With the guard disabled, Envoy preserves the strict aggregate limit but every member has zero effective capacity. - With the guard enabled, every member keeps one token of effective capacity. This avoids a total block, but the aggregate burst can exceed `max_tokens` and the aggregate admitted rate can exceed the configured refill rate. The guard keeps the existing behavior by default so operators can migrate non-zero buckets used as total blocks to `max_tokens: 0` before enabling the change. A permanent configuration option was considered but not added. Zero capacity for a non-zero bucket is a regression, not behavior that should remain part of the long-term API. `max_tokens: 0` now provides an explicit always-reject configuration. The temporary runtime guard gives operators a migration and rollback path without making the accidental behavior permanent. Deployments that require a strict aggregate limit below the local cluster membership need a coordinated global limiter, because independent local buckets cannot both preserve that limit and give every member non-zero capacity. AI assistance was used to trace the regression and prepare the code, regression tests, documentation, and release note. I reviewed and understand the implementation. **Risk Level:** Low while the guard remains disabled by default. Enabling it can admit traffic that the current implementation rejects and can exceed the configured aggregate values when membership is larger than `max_tokens`. **Testing:** Added unit coverage for the guard enabled, the guard disabled, and `max_tokens: 0` with the guard enabled. Envoy's direct format and spelling checks pass. The targeted Bazel build is blocked locally by the host macOS C++ module setup before the changed target compiles, so upstream CI must complete the test. **Docs Changes:** Documented the existing zero-capacity behavior, the guarded minimum-one behavior, and the aggregate capacity tradeoff. **Release Notes:** Added `changelogs/current/bug_fixes/ratelimit__local-cluster-minimum-share.rst` with the guard and migration guidance. **Platform Specific Features:** N/A. **Runtime guard:** `envoy.reloadable_features.local_ratelimit_local_cluster_minimum_one_token`, disabled by default. `false` preserves the current behavior. `true` enables the minimum-one behavior for non-zero buckets. Fixes commit #35207

signals.text: Commit Message: reverse_tunnel: deferred-delete handshake wrappers on host removal Additional Description: When a reverse-tunnel remote host is removed (e.g. cluster host-map update), `removeStaleHostAndCloseConnections` previously closed and immediately destroyed in-flight handshake `RCConnectionWrapper` objects. A late `SimpleConnReadFilter::onData` could then call into `Http1::ConnectionImpl::dispatch` on a freed wrapper/codec (SEGV at faulting address 0x0). This change matches the normal `onConnectionDone` path: shut down the wrapper first (clear the handshake read-filter back-pointer and drop the HTTP/1 codec) and deferred-delete it on the worker dispatcher. AI assistance: used Cursor; I reviewed and understand the change. Removes all hardcoded `envoy` workspace references from test infrastructure so the code works under both WORKSPACE (`TEST_WORKSPACE=envoy`) and bzlmod (`TEST_WORKSPACE=_main`). This is a strict no-op under the current WORKSPACE build. External-repository runfiles mapping (`aws-c-auth-testdata`) is explicitly deferred. No changes to BUILD files, `.bzl` files, or dependency lists. No `BAZEL_CURRENT_REPOSITORY` usage. ### Shell scripts Replace `${TEST_SRCDIR}/envoy` → `${TEST_SRCDIR}/${TEST_WORKSPACE}` across all test shell scripts: - `test/common/runtime/filesystem_setup.sh` - `test/exe/{fips_check,envoy_static_test,version_out_test,pie_test,build_id_test}.sh` - `test/extensions/filters/network/thrift_proxy/driver/generate_fixture.sh` - `test/integration/{hotrestart_test,run_envoy_test,test_utility,sds_dynamic_key_rotation_setup,admin_html/test_server_test}.sh` - `test/tools/router_check/test/route_tests.sh` ### Python test helpers Replace the fragile `TEST_SRCDIR`+workspace-name probe loop with a `__file__`-relative path in `api/tools/generate_listeners_test.py` and `api/tools/tap2pcap_test.py`: ```python # Before: probed TEST_SRCDIR for '_main' or 'envoy_api' subdirectory # After: srcdir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) ``` ### C++ `TestEnvironment` Change `runfilesDirectory` / `runfilesPath` default `workspace` parameter from `"envoy"` to `""`, and resolve the workspace from `TEST_WORKSPACE` at runtime when empty. Falls back to `"envoy"` for non-test / `bazel run` callers: ```cpp // TODO: remove "envoy" fallback once bzlmod migration is complete. const char* ws_env = workspace.empty() ? ::getenv("TEST_WORKSPACE") : nullptr; const std::string& ws = workspace.empty() ? (ws_env != nullptr ? ws_env : "envoy") : workspace; ``` Fix `test/server/config_validation/server_test.cc` call sites that embedded the workspace name in the path: ```cpp // Before: directory_ = TestEnvironment::runfilesDirectory("envoy/test/server/config_validation/test_data/"); // After: directory_ = TestEnvironment::runfilesPath("test/server/config_validation/test_data/"); ```

signals.text: The `corpus_from_config_impl` genrule was non-hermetic (mtimes/uid/gid in tarball varied per machine) and noisy (GNU tar warned about absolute `/tmp/...` paths from the `md5sum | tar -T -` pipeline). ## Changes - **`test/common/router/corpus.bzl`** (new): `corpus_from_test` Starlark rule that uses `ctx.actions.declare_directory` for a reproducible tree artifact and `ctx.actions.run` to invoke the shell script. Plumbs `exec_properties` (a selectable `string_dict`) through as `execution_requirements` on the action, keeping the 6 GiB RBE pool on the expensive step. - **`corpus_from_config_impl.sh`**: Absorbs the normalization and deduplication that was previously inlined in the genrule `cmd` — the two `sed -i` passes plus an in-place `md5sum | sort | awk | xargs rm` dedup that operates entirely within `$GENRULE_OUTPUT_DIR` (no absolute paths). - **`test/common/router/BUILD`**: Replaces the `genrule` with: ```starlark corpus_from_test(name = "corpus_from_config_impl_dir", ...) # tree artifact pkg_files(name = "corpus_from_config_impl_files", srcs = [":corpus_from_config_impl_dir"], strip_prefix = "corpus_from_config_impl_dir") pkg_tar(name = "corpus_from_config_impl", # still produces .tar.gz srcs = [":corpus_from_config_impl_files"], ...) ``` `@rules_pkg` is already a declared dependency of the repo.

signals.text: Two small independent fixes, landed as separate commits. ## Commit 1 — `test/config_test/static_config_validation.py`: catch `yaml.parser.ParserError` `ScannerError` and `ParserError` are sibling PyYAML error types. The script caught `ScannerError` but not `ParserError`, so YAML files that fail at the parse stage (rather than the scan stage) escaped as an uncaught traceback instead of going through the intended `errors` list / "ERROR (validation failed)" path. ```python # Before except (ParseError, KeyError, ScannerError) as e: # After except (ParseError, KeyError, ParserError, ScannerError) as e: ``` Latent bug fix; no behaviour change for any currently-passing input. ## Commit 2 — `ci/format_pre.sh`: add `':!MODULE.bazel'` to git-grep exclusion list Adds `MODULE.bazel` to the pathspec exclusions in `check_legacy_dep_names`. signals.title: dependency: replace bazel-query validate.py with aspect-driven validate_reachability_test
signals.text: `tools/dependency/validate.py` shelled out to `bazel query` 100+ times (once per extension) and scraped repo names with `@(\w+)//`, silently mangling hyphenated/dotted names like `abseil-cpp` → `abseil`. The `@envoy_toolshed` 0.4.6 release (already pinned) ships `dependency/reachability.bzl`, an aspect that computes the full dependency reachability graph once during normal Bazel analysis and emits a single cacheable JSON file. ## Changes - **`tools/dependency/validate_reachability_test.py`** (new): `unittest`-based test that reads three JSON inputs via env vars (`REACHABILITY_JSON`, `REPOSITORY_LOCATIONS_JSON`, `EXTENSIONS_BUILD_CONFIG_JSON`) and runs the same four category checks: `test_only_deps`, `data_plane_core_deps`, `control_plane_deps`, `extension_deps`. Preserves `IGNORE_DEPS`, `implied_untracked_deps` reverse map, and the `boringssl_fips` exclusion. - **`tools/dependency/BUILD`**: loads `dependency_reachability` from `@envoy_toolshed//dependency:reachability.bzl`, adds the rule invocation and a `py_test` wired to `:dep-reachability`, `//bazel:all_repository_locations`, and `//source/extensions:extensions_build_config`. Removes `py_binary` targets for `validate` and `validate_test` and their `aio.api.bazel` / `@envoy_repo` deps. - **`tools/dependency/validate.py`**, **`validate_test.py`**: deleted. - **`ci/do_ci.sh`**: replaces `bazel run //tools/dependency:validate` + `bazel run //tools/dependency:validate_test` with `bazel test //tools/dependency:validate_reachability_test`. ## Behaviour changes (documented in module docstring) **(a) `validate_build_graph_structure` dropped.** The old `deps(//source/...) == deps(core) ∪ deps(//source/extensions/...)` assertion cannot be reconstructed from the reachability JSON, which only covers targets reachable from the declared roots—not the full `//source/...` closure. **(b) `validate_test_only_deps` second direction dropped.** The old check also flagged deps reachable from `//test/...` but not `//source/...` that lacked a `test_only` category (with a `raze__`/`remotejdk`/`_pip3`/`openssl` allowlist). Since `//test/...` is not a declared root in the aspect, test targets do not appear in the reachability data. The first direction—`test_only`-marked deps must not be reachable via a production path—is fully retained.

signals.text: **Commit Message:** postgres_proxy: fix partial initial message leaking to upstream **Additional Description:** Before this PR the postgres_proxy filter forwarded partial bytes of the initial message (SSLRequest or Startup) to upstream when the message arrives split across multiple `onData()` calls. The filter drains the connection buffer and waits for more data. **Risk Level:** Low **Testing:** Unit tests were added. **Release Notes:** Fixed the postgres_proxy filter forwarding incomplete initial message bytes to upstream when the message arrives in multiple TCP segments, causing PostgreSQL to reject the connection.
