signal.title: ci/wasm: Re-enable wasmtime engine tests with hermetic cmake
signal.text: The wasmtime phase of `compile_time_options` has been silently skipped due to an inverted bash check in `ci/do_ci.sh`. Re-enabling it ([failing run](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/actions/runs/28031800806/job/82974411548)) surfaces two breakages that accumulated in the meantime. This PR flips the check and fixes both. ### Re-enable wasmtime tests - `ci/do_ci.sh`: `-z` → `-n` on `ENVOY_SKIP_CTO_WASMTIME`, so the wasmtime phase runs unless explicitly skipped (same flip as on the target branch; will dedupe on merge). ### Hermetic cmake for the wasmtime-c-api-impl build script The crate's `build.rs` spawns `cmake` to install headers, which doesn't exist on the RBE image. Instead of adding cmake to the image, this wires in rules_foreign_cc's prebuilt hermetic cmake toolchain: - New `bazel/wasmtime_c_api_impl.patch` makes `build.rs` honor a `$CMAKE` env var: ```rust let cmake_bin = env::var("CMAKE").unwrap_or_else(|_| "cmake".to_string()); ``` - `bazel/proxy_wasm_cpp_host.patch` extended to apply that patch to the `cu__wasmtime-c-api-impl-45.0.2` crate repo and wire the toolchain into its `cargo_build_script`: ```python build_script_env = {"CMAKE": "$${pwd}/$(CMAKE)"}, toolchains = ["@rules_foreign_cc//toolchains:current_cmake_toolchain"], ``` The toolchain expands `$(CMAKE)` to the exec-root-relative binary path and stages cmake as an action input; rules_rust substitutes `${pwd}` at runtime. - Existing patch sections gained `diff --git` headers — Bazel's patcher mis-applies multi-file unified diffs without them (hunks silently accumulate onto the last-named file). ### Rust 1.88.0 → 1.93.0 The current proxy_wasm_cpp_host pin pulls wasmtime 45.0.2 crates with `rust-version = "1.93.0"`; `wasmtime_environ` fails on 1.88 (E0658 on `fmt::from_fn`). Bumped `rust_register_toolchains` in `bazel/dependency_imports.bzl`. The only other in-repo Rust consumers (dynamic modules SDK/builtin extensions) build cleanly on 1.93. --- 🤖 This PR was created with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot coding agent).

signal.title: docs/bazel: research on keeping hermetic LLVM toolchain working on macOS with LLVM 22
signal.text: macOS CI fails on the LLVM 22 bump (#46297) with the hermetic `toolchains_llvm` toolchain, while the host compiler works. This adds `bazel/llvm-22-macos-hermetic-toolchain.md` with the research requested to establish what is required to keep the hermetic toolchain working. ## Key findings - **Root cause**: `toolchains_llvm` ≤ v1.7.0 on macOS compiles with the hermetic toolchain's bundled libc++ headers but links `-lc++ -lc++abi` from the Xcode SDK sysroot. LLVM 21 moved libc++ hashing out of line (new exported symbol `std::__1::__hash_memory`), so any hermetic LLVM ≥ 21 hits the header/library ABI mismatch: ``` ld64.lld: error: undefined symbol: std::__1::__hash_memory(void const*, unsigned long) >>> referenced by .../abseil-cpp/absl/strings/_objs/cord/cord_analysis.o ``` LLVM 18.1.8 only worked because the version skew was latent. - **Host compiler works** because Apple clang uses the SDK's libc++ headers *and* library — a consistent pair. - **Out-of-band downloads (`extra_llvm_distributions`) are a red herring** — the archive downloads and compiles fine; failure is at link. - **Fixed upstream** in `toolchains_llvm` v1.8.0 (commit `68822c1`, PR bazel-contrib/toolchains_llvm#748, issue #666): macOS now uses the SDK's libc++ end to end, matching host-compiler behavior. ## Options documented - **A (recommended)**: upgrade to toolchains_llvm v1.8.0 — drop `toolchains_llvm_stdc++.patch` (fixed upstream), rebase the toolshed `cxx_cross_lib` patch (needs a new `envoy_toolshed` release; `configure.bzl` was heavily reworked), handle new transitive deps (`helly25_bzl`, `bazel_features` 1.48.1, `rules_cc` 0.2.19), keep `extra_llvm_distributions` for 22.1.8 (v1.8.0's table stops at 22.1.7). - **B**: backport the darwin fix as an extra patch on v1.7.0 (small, but temporary; the upstream commit doesn't apply cleanly). - **C (not recommended)**: per-platform version pinning, static hermetic libc++, or host compiler on macOS. Also documents the consequence: post-fix, macOS builds against the SDK's libc++ (bounded by pinned `XCODE_VERSION`), with only the compiler coming from LLVM 22 — same baseline as the host compiler today. Documentation-only change. Created with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot task agent).
signal.author: Copilot

signal.title: bazel: make toolchains_llvm date-macro redaction configurable via exec-config feature flag
signal.text: `toolchains_llvm` v1.8 unconditionally injects `-imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h` into every C/C++ compile via `unfiltered_compile_flags`. The execroot-relative path resolves fine for normal Bazel `cc` actions but fails in Cargo build-script `cc` invocations (e.g. `ring`) whose working directory isn't the Bazel execroot: ``` cargo:warning=<built-in>:1:19: fatal error: 'external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h' file not found ``` **Design B** — keep redaction ON in target-config compiles (no cache churn), drop it only in exec-config compiles. Bazel resets `--features` → `--host_features` in the exec configuration, so `--host_features=no-redact-dates` naturally scopes the opt-out to build-script `cc` calls without touching target-config action keys. ## Changes - **`bazel/foreign_cc/toolchains_llvm_configurable_redacted_dates.patch`** — patch against pinned `toolchains_llvm` v1.8.0: - Adds `no_redact_dates` `config_setting` to `toolchain/config/BUILD.bazel` matching `values = {"features": "no-redact-dates"}` (same style as existing `use_asan`/`use_ubsan`/`use_tsan`) - Removes the `-Wno-builtin-macro-redefined`/`-imacros`/`redacted_dates_path` lines from the baked `unfiltered_compile_flags` list and builds `redact_dates_flags = select({no_redact_dates: [], default: [redaction flags]})` - Concatenates via `+` at the final `unix_cc_toolchain_config(...)` call site — required because Starlark disallows `list.extend(select(...))`; the earlier `.extend()` calls on `unfiltered_compile_flags` all precede this and remain unaffected - **`bazel/repositories.bzl`** — appends the new patch to `_toolchains_llvm()`'s `patches` list - **`.bazelrc`** — adds `common:clang-common --host_features=no-redact-dates` alongside the existing `compiler-rt=false`/`libunwind=false` lines, scoping the opt-out to exec-config compiles for all clang builds (including RBE `release.test_only`)
signal.author: Copilot

signal.title: bazel: fix `ring` build-script resolution of `redacted_dates.h`
signal.text: `ring`'s `cargo_build_script` inherits the LLVM toolchain's `-imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h` via `rules_rust`'s cc-toolchain wiring, but that execroot-relative path does not resolve from the build script's default run directory. This keeps date redaction fully enabled and instead makes the existing toolchain path resolvable for `ring` only. - **Trace** - `toolchains_llvm` bakes `-Wno-builtin-macro-redefined -imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h` into `unfiltered_compile_flags`. - `rules_rust`'s `cargo_build_script` derives `CC`/`CFLAGS`/`CXXFLAGS` from the cc toolchain and forwards them to `cc-rs`. - As seen in the failing `CargoBuildScriptRun`, `ring` receives: ```text CC=external/llvm_toolchain/bin/cc_wrapper.sh CFLAGS=... -imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h ``` - `redacted_dates.h` is generated in the `@llvm_toolchain` repo and exists in the execroot at `external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h`. - **Change** - Add a crate-universe annotation for `ring` in `/home/runner/work/envoy/envoy/bazel/dependency_imports.bzl`. - Declare `@llvm_toolchain//:redacted_dates.h` as build-script data. - Set the build script `rundir` to `.` so `ring` runs from the execroot, matching the toolchain's relative path. - Regenerate `/home/runner/work/envoy/envoy/Cargo.Bazel.lock` to apply the annotation to `ring`'s generated `cargo_build_script`. - **Why this scope** - No `toolchains_llvm` patch. - No `.bazelrc` / `--host_features` change. - No change to redaction semantics, no absolute paths, no toolchain-wide action rekeying. - Only the affected crate build-script action is adjusted. - **Generated shape** ```starlark "ring": [crate.annotation( build_script_data = ["@llvm_toolchain//:redacted_dates.h"], build_script_rundir = ".", )] ``` - **Problem-statement evidence** - Target/host C++ compile redaction remains intact: representative `CppCompile` `aquery` output is unchanged before/after, including the same `ActionKey` and the same `-imacros external/llvm_toolchain/redacted_dates.h`. - The `ring` fix is localized: its `CargoBuildScriptRun` still carries the same redaction flags; the relevant delta is `--rundir=.` plus the declared header input. - A probe compiled with the LLVM toolchain flags still emits `redacted` for date/time macros rather than real datestamps. - The previously failing `@envoy_rust_crate_index__ring-0.17.14//:_bs` build now succeeds with the toolchain configuration unchanged. - **AI assist** - Copilot assisted with investigation and patch preparation; the change and evidence were reviewed before submission.
signal.author: Copilot

signal.title: Split reverse connection cluster tests into smaller gcc-friendly translation units
signal.text: `reverse_connection_cluster_test.cc` had grown into a single large TU that could time out under gcc on constrained CI workers. This change keeps the test coverage and behavior intact while reducing per-TU compile cost by partitioning the test file into smaller units. - **Shared test scaffold** - Extract the common reverse-connection test infrastructure into `reverse_connection_cluster_test_base.h`. - Move the shared helper and fixtures there: - `TestLoadBalancerContext` - `ReverseConnectionClusterTest` - `UpstreamReverseConnectionAddressTest` - Keep fixture method definitions header-inline so each split TU reuses the same setup without introducing new linkage structure. - **Split by concern** - Replace the monolithic test source with focused TUs: - `reverse_connection_cluster_config_test.cc` - `reverse_connection_cluster_lb_test.cc` - `reverse_connection_cluster_formatter_test.cc` - `reverse_connection_cluster_address_test.cc` - Preserve the existing test cases and assertions; this is a mechanical relocation only. - **Build graph update** - Add a shared `envoy_cc_test_library` for the common header and shared deps. - Replace the single `envoy_cc_test` with one test target per split source. - Keep per-file extras local to the TUs that need them (for example formatter-related stream info mocks and `absl::StrCat`). Example of the new structure: ```starlark envoy_cc_test_library( name = "reverse_connection_cluster_test_base", hdrs = ["reverse_connection_cluster_test_base.h"], deps = [...], ) envoy_cc_test( name = "reverse_connection_cluster_lb_test", srcs = ["reverse_connection_cluster_lb_test.cc"], deps = [":reverse_connection_cluster_test_base"], ) ```

signal.title: ci: auto-label PRs opened against release/v* branches
signal.text: PRs opened against `release/v*` branches should automatically receive `backport` and `changelog-required` labels, with opt-out via `changelog-not-required`. This hooks into the existing `Request` pipeline rather than adding a new `pull_request_target` workflow. ## Changes to `_request.yml` - **`incoming` job — new `Compute labels` step + `labels` output** - Uses the already-pinned `envoyproxy/toolshed/actions/jq` to evaluate target branch and existing PR labels - Emits a compact JSON array (`["backport","changelog-required"]`, `["backport"]`, or `[]`) - `[]` for any non-`release/v*` target; no write permissions here - **New `label` job** (`needs: incoming`) - Only job with `permissions: pull-requests: write`; performs no checkout - Gated on `pull_request_target` + `action == 'opened'` + non-empty `labels` output - Belt-and-suspenders allowlist in the script (`{'backport', 'changelog-required'}`) rejects anything `incoming` might emit outside these two names - Uses `actions/github-script` (already used in this repo, same pinned SHA) to call `addLabels`; errors are caught and surfaced as warnings rather than hard failures ```yaml label: if: >- ${{ (github.repository == 'envoyproxy/envoy' || vars.ENVOY_CI) && github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.action == 'opened' && needs.incoming.outputs.labels != '[]' }} needs: incoming permissions: pull-requests: write steps: - uses: actions/github-script@... with: script: | const ALLOWLIST = new Set(['backport', 'changelog-required']); const labels = JSON.parse('...').filter(l => ALLOWLIST.has(l)); await github.rest.issues.addLabels({ ..., labels }); ``` The `incoming` job carries no write credentials; creds are confined to `label`. Structure is a thin wrapper ready to migrate to a `envoyproxy/toolshed` action later.
signal.author: Copilot

signal.title: bazel(workspace): switch protobuf/protoc to canonical prebuilt toolchain path
signal.text: Envoy’s WORKSPACE path was still using a custom prebuilt-protoc mechanism (`//:protoc` override patch + `com_google_protobuf_protoc_*` repos). This change moves WORKSPACE mode to protobuf’s canonical prebuilt toolchain flow and removes Envoy-specific prebuilt-protoc repo plumbing, without touching bzlmod/MODULE behavior. - **WORKSPACE toolchain wiring** - Added `bazel/protobuf_toolchains.bzl` and invoked it from `WORKSPACE` after `com_google_protobuf` is available. - Instantiates `@prebuilt_protoc.<platform>` repos from protobuf’s `PROTOBUF_PLATFORMS` via `prebuilt_protoc_repo`. - Registers protobuf prebuilt toolchains: - `@com_google_protobuf//bazel/private/oss/toolchains/prebuilt:all` - Enabled workspace flag in `.bazelrc`: - `--@com_google_protobuf//bazel/flags:prefer_prebuilt_protoc=true` - **Remove Envoy home-grown prebuilt-protoc machinery** - Dropped `PROTOC_VERSIONS` and `_compiled_protoc_deps` from `bazel/repository_locations.bzl`. - Removed creation of `com_google_protobuf_protoc_*` repos from `bazel/repositories.bzl`. - Removed corresponding `com_google_protobuf_protoc_*` metadata from `bazel/deps.yaml`. - Removed protobuf patch hunk that rewired `//:protoc` to Envoy-managed prebuilt repos. - **Patch updates retained for WORKSPACE correctness** - Kept unrelated/required protobuf patch hunks (`cpp_opts`, zlib label mapping). - Added `bazel/protobuf_prebuilt_tool_integrity.patch` so WORKSPACE tarball builds have complete v35.1 prebuilt protoc integrity entries across protobuf’s platform set. - **Direct protoc invocation audit + handling** - Added Envoy-owned stable shim target `//bazel:protoc` for direct label-style consumers that can use file-backed tool selection. - Repointed `bazel/envoy_build_system.bzl` descriptor genrule path to `@envoy//bazel:protoc`. - Kept executable-attr direct consumers (`tools/api_proto_plugin/plugin.bzl`, `api/bazel/cc_proto_descriptor_library/builddefs.bzl`) on `@com_google_protobuf//:protoc` to preserve executable-target semantics and avoid breakage. ```starlark # bazel/BUILD alias( name = "protoc", actual = select({ ":linux_x86_64": "@prebuilt_protoc.linux_x86_64//:bin/protoc", ":darwin_arm64": "@prebuilt_protoc.osx_aarch_64//:bin/protoc", ":windows_x86_64": "@prebuilt_protoc.win64//:bin/protoc.exe", "//conditions:default": "@com_google_protobuf//:protoc", }), ) ```

signal.title: distribution: fix proxy-responds test to assert HTTP status instead of stale homepage copy
signal.text: The `proxy-responds` test in `distribution/distrotest.sh` was greping the `www.envoyproxy.io` response body for a hardcoded tagline that no longer exists on the homepage, causing every distro/package combination in `verify_distro` to permafail. ## Change Replace the body-content grep with a `curl -sf` status-code assertion, decoupling CI from website copy entirely: ```shell # Before RESPONSE="$(retry 60 curl -s http://localhost:10000/)" echo "$RESPONSE" | grep "Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy, designed for cloud-native applications" # After — assert HTTP 2xx, not homepage copy RESPONSE="$(retry 60 curl -s http://localhost:10000/)" retry 60 curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:10000/ ``` - `RESPONSE` is still captured so `dump_envoy_response` retains diagnostic output on failure - `retry 60` is preserved for upstream flakiness handling - `curl -f` returns non-zero on HTTP ≥ 400, correctly tripping the ERR trap on genuine proxy failures

signal.title: socket_interface: gate sockmap off non-linux
signal.text: The sockmap socket interface was registered unconditionally, so macOS and Windows still pulled its config and stub datapath into `all_extensions_lib`/`envoy-static`. That also prevented the Linux-only leaf targets from using `target_compatible_with` without breaking explicit `envoy-static` builds off Linux. - **Registration path** - Keep the extension entry in `source/extensions/extensions_build_config.bzl` unchanged so extension tooling continues to see a static registry. - Make `//source/extensions/network/socket_interface/sockmap:config` follow the existing platform-gated extension pattern: on Linux it builds normally; off Linux it resolves to an empty extension target. - **Linux-only targets** - Add `target_compatible_with = ["@platforms//os:linux"]` to the sockmap-only implementation targets: - `sockmap_bpf` - `bpf_datapath_lib` - `io_handle_lib` - This restores correct `bazel build //...` skipping semantics on non-Linux once the registration edge is severed. - **Stub behavior** - Keep the `#ifdef ENVOY_ENABLE_SOCKMAP` / `#else` split in `bpf_datapath.cc`. - The stub is still needed for Linux builds where the extension is compiled but `--define sockmap=enabled` is not set. Example of the config gating applied in `sockmap/BUILD`: ```starlark envoy_cc_extension( name = "config", srcs = select({ "//bazel:linux": ["socket_interface.cc"], "//conditions:default": [], }), hdrs = select({ "//bazel:linux": ["socket_interface.h"], "//conditions:default": [], }), deps = select({ "//bazel:linux": [ ":bpf_datapath_lib", ":io_handle_lib", # ... ], "//conditions:default": [], }), ) ```
signal.author: Copilot

signal.title: test: replace hardcoded workspace name "envoy" with TEST_WORKSPACE

This is a strict no-op under the current WORKSPACE build. External-repository runfiles mapping (`aws-c-auth-testdata`) is explicitly deferred. No changes to BUILD files, `.bzl` files, or dependency lists. No `BAZEL_CURRENT_REPOSITORY` usage. ### Shell scripts Replace `${TEST_SRCDIR}/envoy` → `${TEST_SRCDIR}/${TEST_WORKSPACE}` across all test shell scripts: - `test/common/runtime/filesystem_setup.sh` - `test/exe/{fips_check,envoy_static_test,version_out_test,pie_test,build_id_test}.sh` - `test/extensions/filters/network/thrift_proxy/driver/generate_fixture.sh` - `test/integration/{hotrestart_test,run_envoy_test,test_utility,sds_dynamic_key_rotation_setup,admin_html/test_server_test}.sh` - `test/tools/router_check/test/route_tests.sh` ### Python test helpers Replace the fragile `TEST_SRCDIR`+workspace-name probe loop with a `__file__`-relative path in `api/tools/generate_listeners_test.py` and `api/tools/tap2pcap_test.py`: ```python # Before: probed TEST_SRCDIR for '_main' or 'envoy_api' subdirectory # After: srcdir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) ``` ### C++ `TestEnvironment` Change `runfilesDirectory` / `runfilesPath` default `workspace` parameter from `"envoy"` to `""`, and resolve the workspace from `TEST_WORKSPACE` at runtime when empty. Falls back to `"envoy"` for non-test / `bazel run` callers: ```cpp // TODO: remove "envoy" fallback once bzlmod migration is complete. const char* ws_env = workspace.empty() ? ::getenv("TEST_WORKSPACE") : nullptr; const std::string& ws = workspace.empty() ? (ws_env != nullptr ? ws_env : "envoy") : workspace; ``` Fix `test/server/config_validation/server_test.cc` call sites that embedded the workspace name in the path: ```cpp // Before: directory_ = TestEnvironment::runfilesDirectory("envoy/test/server/config_validation/test_data/"); // After: directory_ = TestEnvironment::runfilesPath("test/server/config_validation/test_data/"); ```

signal.title: router: replace corpus_from_config_impl genrule with hermetic Starlark rule + pkg_tar
signal.text: The `corpus_from_config_impl` genrule was non-hermetic (mtimes/uid/gid in tarball varied per machine) and noisy (GNU tar warned about absolute `/tmp/...` paths from the `md5sum | tar -T -` pipeline). ## Changes - **`test/common/router/corpus.bzl`** (new): `corpus_from_test` Starlark rule that uses `ctx.actions.declare_directory` for a reproducible tree artifact and `ctx.actions.run` to invoke the shell script. Preserves `cfg = "target"` on the test binary for oss-fuzz host/target correctness. Plumbs `exec_properties` (a selectable `string_dict`) through as `execution_requirements` on the action, keeping the 6 GiB RBE pool on the expensive step. - **`corpus_from_config_impl.sh`**: Absorbs the normalization and deduplication that was previously inlined in the genrule `cmd` — the two `sed -i` passes plus an in-place `md5sum | sort | awk | xargs rm` dedup that operates entirely within `$GENRULE_OUTPUT_DIR` (no absolute paths). - **`test/common/router/BUILD`**: Replaces the `genrule` with: ```starlark corpus_from_test(name = "corpus_from_config_impl_dir", ...) # tree artifact pkg_files(name = "corpus_from_config_impl_files", srcs = [":corpus_from_config_impl_dir"], strip_prefix = "corpus_from_config_impl_dir") pkg_tar(name = "corpus_from_config_impl", # still produces .tar.gz srcs = [":corpus_from_config_impl_files"], ...) ``` `@rules_pkg` is already a declared dependency of the repo.
signal.author: Copilot

signal.title: config_test/ci: catch ParserError in static_config_validation; pre-exclude MODULE.bazel from format_pre grep
signal.text: Two small independent fixes, landed as separate commits. ## Commit 1 — `test/config_test/static_config_validation.py`: catch `yaml.parser.ParserError` `ScannerError` and `ParserError` are sibling PyYAML error types. The script caught `ScannerError` but not `ParserError`, so YAML files that fail at the parse stage (rather than the scan stage) escaped as an uncaught traceback instead of going through the intended `errors` list / "ERROR (validation failed)" path. ```python # Before except (ParseError, KeyError, ScannerError) as e: # After except (ParseError, KeyError, ParserError, ScannerError) as e: ``` Latent bug fix; no behaviour change for any currently-passing input. ## Commit 2 — `ci/format_pre.sh`: add `':!MODULE.bazel'` to git-grep exclusion list Adds `MODULE.bazel` to the pathspec exclusions in `check_legacy_dep_names`. The file does not exist at the repo root on `main` yet, so this change is currently inert — it is groundwork for the bzlmod migration so the eventual flip PR does not need to touch unrelated CI scripting.
signal.author: Copilot

signal.title: dependency: replace bazel-query validate.py with aspect-driven validate_reachability_test
signal.text: `tools/dependency/validate.py` shelled out to `bazel query` 100+ times (once per extension) and scraped repo names with `@(\w+)//`, silently mangling hyphenated/dotted names like `abseil-cpp` → `abseil`. The `@envoy_toolshed` 0.4.6 release (already pinned) ships `dependency/reachability.bzl`, an aspect that computes the full dependency reachability graph once during normal Bazel analysis and emits a single cacheable JSON file. ## Changes - **`tools/dependency/validate_reachability_test.py`** (new): `unittest`-based test that reads three JSON inputs via env vars (`REACHABILITY_JSON`, `REPOSITORY_LOCATIONS_JSON`, `EXTENSIONS_BUILD_CONFIG_JSON`) and runs the same four category checks: `test_only_deps`, `data_plane_core_deps`, `control_plane_deps`, `extension_deps`. Preserves `IGNORE_DEPS`, `implied_untracked_deps` reverse map, and the `boringssl_fips` exclusion. - **`tools/dependency/BUILD`**: loads `dependency_reachability` from `@envoy_toolshed//dependency:reachability.bzl`, adds the rule invocation and a `py_test` wired to `:dep-reachability`, `//bazel:all_repository_locations`, and `//source/extensions:extensions_build_config`. Removes `py_binary` targets for `validate` and `validate_test` and their `aio.api.bazel` / `@envoy_repo` deps. - **`tools/dependency/validate.py`**, **`validate_test.py`**: deleted. - **`ci/do_ci.sh`**: replaces `bazel run //tools/dependency:validate` + `bazel run //tools/dependency:validate_test` with `bazel test //tools/dependency:validate_reachability_test`. ## Behaviour changes (documented in module docstring) **(a) `validate_build_graph_structure` dropped.** The old `deps(//source/...) == deps(core) ∪ deps(//source/extensions/...)` assertion cannot be reconstructed from the reachability JSON, which only covers targets reachable from the declared roots—not the full `//source/...` closure. **(b) `validate_test_only_deps` second direction dropped.** The old check also flagged deps reachable from `//test/...` but not `//source/...` that lacked a `test_only` category (with a `raze__`/`remotejdk`/`_pip3`/`openssl` allowlist). Since `//test/...` is not a declared root in the aspect, test targets do not appear in the reachability data. The first direction—`test_only`-marked deps must not be reachable via a production path—is fully retained.
signal.author: Copilot

signal.title: [WIP] Fix hardcoded re2 dependency in pgv_cc_proto_library
signal.text: Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress. > ## Background > > Envoy's in-tree `bazel/pgv.patch` patches `protoc-gen-validate`'s `pgv_cc_proto_library` by **hardcoding** the re2 dependency to `@re2`: > > ```diff > --- a/bazel/pgv_proto_library.bzl > +++ b/bazel/pgv_proto_library.bzl > @@ -48,7 +48,7 @@ def pgv_cc_proto_library( > "@com_envoyproxy_protoc_gen_validate//validate:cc_validate", > "@com_envoyproxy_protoc_gen_validate//validate:validate_cc", > "@com_google_protobuf//:protobuf", > - "@com_googlesource_code_re2//:re2", > + "@re2", > ], > ``` > > This works in WORKSPACE mode only because Envoy's WORKSPACE happens to create a repo literally named `re2`. It is not portable — under bzlmod the apparent repo name is determined by the module graph, so a hardcoded `@re2` inside the patched dependency's own `.bzl` does not resolve correctly. > > The `envoyproxy/bazel-registry` module `protoc-gen-validate/1.3.0.envoy` already solves this properly by **parameterising** the deps instead of hardcoding them, so the *caller* injects the correct label: > > https://github.com/envoyproxy/bazel-registry/blob/main/modules/protoc-gen-validate/1.3.0.envoy/patches/pgv.patch > > ```diff > --- a/bazel/pgv_proto_library.bzl > +++ b/bazel/pgv_proto_library.bzl > @@ -22,6 +22,8 @@ def pgv_cc_proto_library( > deps = [], > cc_deps = [], > copts = [], > + re2 = None, > + protobuf = None, > **kargs): > """Bazel rule to create a C++ protobuf validation library from proto source files > Args: > @@ -47,8 +49,8 @@ def pgv_cc_proto_library( > ":" + name + "_cc_proto", > "@com_envoyproxy_protoc_gen_validate//validate:cc_validate", > "@com_envoyproxy_protoc_gen_validate//validate:validate_cc", > - "@com_google_protobuf//:protobuf", > - "@com_googlesource_code_re2//:re2", > + protobuf or "@com_google_protobuf//:protobuf", > + re2 or "@com_googlesource_code_re2//:re2", > ], > copts = copts + select({ > "@com_envoyproxy_protoc_gen_validate//bazel:windows_x86_64": ["-DWIN32"], > ``` > > This is a prerequisite for the ongoing bzlmod migration (#42890). Converging the in-tree patch with the registry patch now means both build modes go through an identical code path, and there is no silent behaviour change when the in-tree patch is eventually deleted. > > ## Task > > ### 1. Replace `bazel/pgv.patch` with the parameterised form > > Rewrite `bazel/pgv.patch` so that the `bazel/pgv_proto_library.bzl` hunk matches the registry patch above: > > - Add `re2 = None` and `protobuf = None` keyword parameters to `pgv_cc_proto_library`. > - Replace the hardcoded `"@com_google_protobuf//:protobuf"` and `"@com_googlesource_code_re2//:re2"` deps entries with `protobuf or "@com_google_protobuf//:protobuf"` and `re2 or "@com_googlesource_code_re2//:re2"` respectively. > - Do **not** keep the `-"@com_googlesource_code_re2//:re2"` / `+"@re2"` hardcoded substitution — it is replaced by the parameterisation. > > Note the base blob is the same (`index b8fb865..`) for both the current in-tree patch and the registry patch, so the new hunk should apply cleanly against the pinned `com_envoyproxy_protoc_gen_validate` version in `api/bazel/repository_locations.bzl` (currently v1.3.3). Please verify this. > > ### 2. Keep the `bazel/protobuf.bzl` hunk, but clean it up > > The second hunk in `bazel/pgv.patch` patches `bazel/protobuf.bzl`: > > - **Keep** the `_validate_deps` change (`Label("@com_googlesource_code_re2//:re2")` → `Label("@re2")`) unless a cleaner parameterisation is straightforward — this is a rule attribute default, not a macro argument, so it cannot be injected by the caller in the same way. If the registry patch handles this differently, match the registry's approach. > - **Remove the no-op `_protoc` hunk.** The current patch contains: > ```diff > "_protoc": attr.label( > cfg = "exec", > - default = Label("@com_google_protobuf//:protoc"), > + default = Label("@com_google_protobuf//:protoc"), > ``` > Both sides are byte-identical — this is leftover noise from a reverted rename and should be dropped. > > ### 3. Update the call site in `api/bazel/api_build_system.bzl` > > In `api_cc_py_proto_library`, pass the re2 label explicitly to `pgv_cc_proto_library`: > > ```starlark > pgv_cc_proto_library( > name = cc_proto_library_name, > linkstatic = linkstatic, > cc_deps = [...], > deps = [relative_name], > re2 = "@re2", > visibility = ["//visibility:public"], > ) > ``` > > This keeps WORKSPACE-mode resolution exactly as it is today (`@re2` is the repo Envoy's WORKSPACE creates), while making the dependency caller-injected so the same call site works under bzlmod. > > ## Constraints / notes > > - **This must not change behaviour in WORKSPACE mode.** The resulting `cc_library` deps for every `pgv_cc_proto_library` target must be identical before and after this change. Please confirm by inspecting the generated deps if practical. > - Do **not** modify `api/bazel/repositories.bzl` or `api/bazel/repository_locations.bzl` — those are being handled separately. > - Do **not** enable bzlmod or touch `.bazelrc`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `MODULE.bazel.lock`. > - The default values in the patch (`"@com_google_protobuf//:protobuf"` / `"@com_googlesource_code_re2//:re2"`) are never exercised by Envoy in either mode; they exist purely to keep the patch upstream-compatible. Preserve them as-is. > > ## Validation > > - `bazel build //api/...` (or a representative subset such as `//api/envoy/config/core/v3:pkg_cc_proto`) should succeed in the default WORKSPACE mode. > - The patch must apply cleanly — check for `Patch failed` / offset warnings during the `com_envoyproxy_protoc_gen_validate` fetch. > - Run the repo's format/lint tooling over any modified Starlark. > > > The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated): > > User: so im looking to land this asap - the last commit is the only relevant one (other commits are part of pre prs) > > essentially the plan is for a hard migration, but to have a brief moment of bzlmod/workspace compat to allow the transition > > trying to see what in this commmit can be landed in workspacce mode without breaking it or with minimal adaptation > > Assistant: Here's my triage of `f22a31f` ("bazel: Enable bzlmod"), split by what can land now in WORKSPACE mode vs. what must wait for the flip. > > ## ✅ Land now — no WORKSPACE impact > > | Change | Why it's safe | > |---|---| > | `BUILD`: `exports_files([... "MODULE.bazel.lock" ...])` | Inert in WORKSPACE mode; just makes the lock addressable. | > | `bazel/repository_locations_aliases.bzl` (new `MODULE_NAME_ALIASES`) | Pure data file, no loaders depend on it yet. Land it standalone. | > | `bazel/extensions.bzl` (new) | Module extensions are never evaluated in WORKSPACE mode. But **must** land together with the `bazel/BUILD` jq rework or dep checks break — see below. | > | `ci/do_ci.sh`: `bazel query --consistent_labels` + deriving repo name from the label instead of hardcoding `envoy_api~` / `envoy_api` | This is strictly *better* in WORKSPACE mode — `--consistent_labels` normalises to `@@envoy_api//` in both modes and the derived `INPUT_DIR` works for canonical names. signal.title: Use PassthroughState pointer value as thread local storage key for peer metadata exchange
signal.text: Commit Message: This pull request introduces a new mechanism for Istio peer_metadata filters communicating across an internal socket/listener to exchange peer metadata information through thread local storage. The previous implementation would do inject peer metadata into the data stream directly, but that does not work when internal transport socket wraps a PROXY or TLS socket because those aren't prepared to use handle the arbitrary data injected into the data stream. To fix that problem we tried to use thread local storage instead of injecting data into the data stream and used downstream connection ID as a shared key in the thread local storage that both filters are aware of, but that approach does not work well when multiple requests are multiplexed over the same downstream HTTP2 connection - they would share the same downstream connection ID and will use the same key for thread local storage, even if the destinations are different. The new implementation in this PR uses thread local storage, just like the approach above, but instead of using downstream connection ID it uses PassthroughState pointer value as a key. PassthroughState pointer is basically allocated per upstream connection, so that addresses the issue with multiplexed requests - as we get a unique key per upstream connection after endpoint selection and multiplexing decisions have been made already. Additional Description: Risk Level: low - feature is specific to Istio and does not touch core Envoy, and it's disabled by default. Testing: integration tests Docs Changes: n/a Release Notes: n/a Platform Specific Features: n/a

signal.title: Introduce StringMatcher to the compressor
signal.text: Commit Message: This PR adds new functionality of the compressor module to allow usage of StringMatcher, to allow more than just exact match for the content_type as it is at the moment. Additional Description: Current state of compressor allows only to use exact match for content types or it will fallback to the default list. There is no way how to specify wildcards to allow extreme amount of different content types as it is in our case. Generative AI has been used. Risk Level: Medium Testing: In addition to the written tests in the PR I have compiled the proxy locally, started up the proxy and tested against multiple envoy proxy configurations to prove envoy StringMatcher is supported and response is compressed while original logic of exact match and default list still function correctly. Docs Changes: New field content_type_matcher introduced for the compressor Release Notes: compressor: added support for ``content_type_matcher`` in ``CommonDirectionConfig``, allowing fine-grained MIME type matching via string matchers. [Optional Fixes #Issue] Fixes https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/issues/46344 FYI: Original PR was https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/pull/46374 where I was told to introduce StringMatcher into the compressor hence here is the new suggested solution.

signal.title: postgres_proxy: fix partial initial message leaking to upstream
signal.text: **Commit Message:** postgres_proxy: fix partial initial message leaking to upstream **Additional Description:** Before this PR the postgres_proxy filter forwarded partial bytes of the initial message (SSLRequest or Startup) to upstream when the message arrives split across multiple `onData()` calls. The upstream PostgreSQL server received an incomplete message fragment and logs an error. This PR changes the decoder logic to return `Stopped` when processing incomplete initial message, which avoids forwarding the incomplete data to the next filter. The filter drains the connection buffer and waits for more data. **Risk Level:** Low **Testing:** Unit tests were added. **Release Notes:** Fixed the postgres_proxy filter forwarding incomplete initial message bytes to upstream when the message arrives in multiple TCP segments, causing PostgreSQL to reject the connection. Fixes #46774
signal.author: tsaarni

signal.title: reverse_tunnel: deferred-delete handshake wrappers on host removal
signal.text: Commit Message: reverse_tunnel: deferred-delete handshake wrappers on host removal Additional Description: When a reverse-tunnel remote host is removed (e.g. cluster host-map update), `removeStaleHostAndCloseConnections` previously closed and immediately destroyed in-flight handshake `RCConnectionWrapper` objects. A late `SimpleConnReadFilter::onData` could then call into `Http1::ConnectionImpl::dispatch` on a freed wrapper/codec (SEGV at faulting address 0x0). This change matches the normal `onConnectionDone` path: shut down the wrapper first (clear the handshake read-filter back-pointer and drop the HTTP/1 codec) and deferred-delete it on the worker dispatcher. AI assistance: used Cursor; I reviewed and understand the change. Risk Level: Low Testing: Extended `RemoveStaleHostAndCloseConnections` and added `SimpleConnReadFilterTest.OnDataAfterClearParent`; please rely on CI for full format/tests. Docs Changes: N/A Release Notes: changelogs/current/bug_fixes/reverse_tunnel__deferred-delete-stale-handshake-wrappers.rst
